records.title: TRAFFICKING OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN .
details:
(a) whether attention of Government has been brought to a recent
 report published in the print media regarding trafficking of
 women and children in the country, sponsored by National Human
 Rights Commission, which has pointed that India is slowly turning
 into a centre for child-sex tourists;
(b) whether Government are also aware that the problem is more
 acute in India’s popular tourist destinations including Goa and
 Kerala;
(c) if so, whether Government have taken any steps to prevent
 children from sexual abuse in these tourist circuits;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY)
(a)&(b) As per the Report of Action research on Trafficking in
Women and Children, August 2004 sponsored by National Human
Rights Commission, child sex tourism is prevalent in India and
also in the States of Goa and Kerala.
(c)&(d) the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956 (ITPA)
supplemented by the Indian Penal Code prohibits trafficking in
human beings including children for purpose of prostitution and
lays down severe penalties for traffickers. The ITPA is now
being further amended providing for more stringent punishment for
trafficking in persons including children. The Ministry of Women
and Child Development conducts advocacy, awareness generation,
sensitization programmes for prevention of child trafficking.
The Central Advisory Committee on combating Child Prostitution
headed by Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development,
Government of India reviews the State’s activities in combating
trafficking and prostitution every quarter. The Ministry of
Women and Child Development also runs Swadhar shelter Homes which
provide shelter, food, clothing, emotional support, counseling,
rehabilitation and other facilities to sex workers including
children.
(e) Does not arise.

records.title: FRESH APPROVALS FOR FIELD TRIALS OF GM CROPS
details:
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI A. RAJA) 
(a) to (d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFFERED TO IN THE REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION 
NO. 246 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING “FRESH APPROVALS FOR FIELD TRIALS OF GM CROPS” DUE
FOR REPLY ON 8.12.2006.
(a) The Government of India has not approved any fresh field trials on transgenic crops,
after the Supreme Court direction dated 22.9.2006 However, field trials for transgenic 
mustard developed by University of Delhi South Campus, New Delhi have been permitted as per
Hon’ble Supreme Court order dated 13.10.2006 passed on an appeal filed by Delhi University.
(b) to (d) There is no proposal to direct independent inquiry into the long term economic 
viability of GM crops in the Indian environment. 
As per the prevailing statutory rules, procedures and guidelines under the Rules for the 
Manufacture, Use/Import/Export and Storage of Hazardous Micro Organisms/ Genetically 
Engineered Organisms or Cells, 1989 notified under the Environmental (Protection) Act, 1986,
the safety, efficacy, agronomic advantage and economic viability of the introduced trait in 
GM crops are assessed on a case to case basis by the regulatory agencies prior to according 
environmental release of the product. No prior determination that GM crops in general or a 
specific GM crop in particular, is, or is not viable in Indian 
conditions is scientifically defensible. The evidence has to be generated, and evaluated 
in each case in the Indian context, through properly defined Protocols.

records.title: SMUGGLING OF RDX .
details:
(a) the total number of cases of RDX seizures made by Indian security forces during the preceding year, and the total quantity of RDX thus recovered; 
(b) whether it is a fact that a majority of RDX thus seized is being smuggled into country, because a majority of airports in India lack suitable equipment to scan and detect RDX; and
(c) if so, what steps Government propose to take to prevent inbound smuggling of RDX 
at all entry points of the country?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)
(a): As per information available with this Ministry, 1021 Kgs. (Approx.) of RDX were seized by Police and security forces in different parts of the country in 2005, while in 2006 (till October), 724 Kgs.(Approx.) of RDX were seized. 
(b): There are no inputs to suggest that the RDX so seized were smuggled into the country through the Airports.
(c): The necessary steps have been taken to enhance surveillance and physical security and scanning of baggage at the Airports. The security of a large number of Airports is now looked after by CISF. The Government has also initiated several measures to prevent smuggling of arms, ammunition and explosives from across the borders, which inter-alia include i) ongoing fencing of Eastern and Western borders, ii) deployment of border guarding forces, iii) strengthening of intelligence capacity along the borders, iv) periodic sensitization of Border Guarding Forces and the State governments particularly in the border states, v) strengthening of coastal security, etc.

records.title: DIFFERENTIAL TARIFF FOR ELECTRICITY .
details:
(a) whether Government have any proposal to divide the electricity consumption in 
the country into peak and off-peak hours, with electricity costing cheaper during the off-
peak hours; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )
(a) & (b) : A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 180 TO BE ANSWERED IN THE RAJYA 
SABHA ON 04.12.2006 REGARDING DIFFERENTIAL TARIFF FOR 
ELECTRICITY.
(a) & (b): The National Electricity Policy seeks to encourage reduction of the 
difference between electrical power demand during peak periods and off-peak 
periods in order to reduce the requirements for capacity additions. It states that 
differential tariff structure for peak and off peak supply and metering 
arrangements (Time of Day metering) would be conducive to load management 
objectives. TOD meters for large consumers with a minimum load of one MVA 
are sought to encourage in the first instance. 
 The Tariff Policy requires the State Electricity Regulatory 
Commissions to introduce two-part tariffs featuring separate fixed and variable 
charges and time differentiated tariff on priority for large consumers (consumers 
with demand exceeding 1 MW) within one year. This would also help in flattening 
the peak and implementing various energy conservation measures. 
 Wherever such differential tariff is introduced, it would naturally 
involve higher tariffs during peaking hours and lower tariffs during off-peak 
hours.

records.title: PREVENTION OF BIRD FLU AMONG THE HUMAN BEINGS .
details:
(a) whether Government have any contingency plan ready to prevent the reoccurrence of bird 
flu virus in the human population in the country in the coming months;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE 
(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)
(a) Yes, Sir.
(b) & (c) Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India has a contingency plan
to manage human cases of Avian Influenza. The plan includes active surveillance, preventive 
public health measures, clinical management, stockpiling of specific drugs, personal 
protective equipments and IEC activities.
 This plan was operationalized during the outbreak of Avian Flue among poultry in
Nundurbar and Jalgaon districts of Maharasthra, Surat District of Gujarat and Burhanpur
district of Madhya Pradesh in February-April, 2006. Due to the coordinated action no 
human case of avian influenza was reported. This contingency plan would hold good for 
any reoccurrence of bird flu in human population in the country.

records.title: LIMITING OF FERTILIZER SUBSIDY .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that the fertilizer subsidy burden on Government 
have touched a whopping Rs.32,840 crores against the budgeted 
Rs.18,752 crores during the current fiscal;
(b) if so, whether Government propose to take any action to limit the 
subsidy expenditure; and
(c) If so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS.
(SHRI B.K.HANDIQUE)
(a) The requirement of funds for subsidy on sale of fertilizers during 2006-07 is 
estimated at Rs.27039.00 crore and in addition, there was a carry-over liability from the 
previous year of Rs.5913.94 crore increasing the total requirement to Rs.32952.94 crores in 
the current year. Department of Fertilizers has till now received Rs.18752.91 crore for 
payment of subsidy in the current year. 
(b) & (c). The increase in subsidy expenditure is due to the increase in consumption of 
fertilizers within the country coupled with the increase in cost of fertilizer due to increase in 
raw material cost in the international market. The Department is making efforts to 
encourage the Indian industry to set up Joint Ventures in raw material resource rich 
countries to ensure sustained availability of inputs and finished fertilizers in the country at 
reasonable prices. It is expected that Indian investment in fertilizer sector abroad and will 
ensure long-term supplies of raw materials/finished fertilizers to the country as also help in 
stabilizing the volatility of the prices in the international market.
 The New Pricing Scheme for Urea units in the country also lays emphasis on 
maximizing indigenous production with energy efficiency and competitiveness at global 
standards. This will also help in controlling subsidy expenditure.

records.title: REDUCTION IN TRANSACTION COSTS FOR EXPORTS .
details:
MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
( SHRI KAMAL NATH )
(a) to (d) Indian exporters may have to incur higher transaction costs as compared to other developed countries. 
Government has taken several steps to reduce the transaction costs and to simplify the procedures. It is a continuous and ongoing exercise. To make the Export Promotion schemes user friendly, major simplification of procedures has been introduced. records.title: DROP OUT RATE OF GIRL STUDENTS
details:
MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI ARJUN SINGH)
(a) to (d) : A statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
STATEMENT
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (d) OF THE RAJYA
SABHA STARRED QUESTION N0. 63 FOR ANSWER ON 27.11.2006
ASKED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA REGARDING ` DROP-OUT OF GIRL
STUDENTS `
(a): In 2003-04, the drop-out rates for` girl students in the country as a whole at the primary stage (Classes I-V), at elementary stage (Classes I-VIII) and Secondary stage (Classes I-X) were 28.6%, 52.9% and 64.9% respectively . At the primary stage, the drop-out rate for girls was lower than that of boys, whereas for elementary and secondary stages, they were higher than that of boys. 
(b),(c) & (d): Under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, a multi-pronged approach has been adopted for reducing drop-out rates. One set of interventions relates to strengthening of primary and upper primary schools and improving the quality of education through improvement in school infrastructure, recruitment of additional teachers, annual school grants, regular training of teachers, introduction of good and innovative teaching practices that make class rooms more joyful and attractive regular academic support to teachers, etc. On the other hand, several interventions aim at improving the demand for schooling through community mobilization, special interventions for enrolment and retention of vulnerable groups of children including girls and children of weaker sections. Measures are also being undertaken to strengthen the accountability of the school system towards parents and the community. The Mid-Day Meal Scheme that: provides a cooked meal to all children of Government and Government-aided primary schools, Education Guarantee Scheme (EGS) Centers and Alternative & Innovative Education (AIE) centers, also has the potential for promoting school enrolment and participation.
Free textbooks are provided to all girls and all SC & ST students up to the elementary stage. Under the National Programme for Education of Girls of the Elementary Level (NPEGEL), additional resources are provided to 3164 educationally backward blocks for interventions of community mobilization, bridge courses for out-of-school girls, strengthening of model cluster schools, gender sensitization of teachers etc. to promote retention of girls in primary and upper primary schools. 1000 Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBV) which are residential schools for girls at upper primary level, particularly for girls from disadvantaged sections of society, have been approved in the current year besides 1180 KGBVs sanctioned earlier in educationally backward blocks of the country.
As per a new Scholarship scheme introduced by Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) from the academic session 2006-07, a girl who is the only child of her parent, and who secures 60% or more marks in class X examination for the year 2006 onwards under C3SE system, would be given a scholarship of Rs.500 per month for studying in classes XI and X]II in a CBSE affiliated school which charges tuition fee of not more than Rs. 1000 per month.
All Kendriya Vidyalayas provide fee waiver to single girl children
from classes VI to XII.
In Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, one third of the seats are reserved for girls.

records.title: WORKING CONDITIONS IN SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH ESTABLISHMENTS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that lack of good research facilities and poor
working conditions including low salaries in the country`s major
scientific research establishments is the major reason for fewer students
opting for science courses at the college level this year;
(b) if so, the details of any corrective action Government plans to take
in this regard; and
(c) the details of steps taken by Government to improve the work
environment at our scientific research establishments?

MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF EARTH SCIENCES 
(KAPIL SIBAL)
(a) to (c): No Sir. The students` choice to take admission in various
science courses is driven by other avenues available in the country. This
is a cyclical phenomenon and is in response to the available employment
opportunities in various other sectors. The Government have taken various
corrective measures like enhanced research infrastructure in the
universities for better training of students, adoption of new syllabi to
match the global changes, special schemes for attracting students to
science streams, etc. The salary of a scientist employed in a Government
funded institute cannot be comparable to that in private funded
organizations in the country.
Science is driven by individual passion and commitment and not
necessarily by monetary benefits. However, a reasonable minimum level of
good research facilities and better working conditions and associated
perquisites will greatly improve the present situation. The Government
has doubled the funding for science and technology in the 10th Plan and
the same will be further enhanced in 11th Plan.

records.title: PROJECT FOR STRENGHENING WESTERN GRID .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government have approved a project for strengthening of 
western grid in the country;
(b) if so, the details of the project and the estimated date of its completion; and
(c) the details of the benefits accruing to Maharashtra following the project`s completion?

THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE )
(a) to (c) : Yes, Sir. Investment approval has been issued for `Western Region System 
Strengthening Scheme-II` of Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) on 24th July, 
2006. The estimated cost of the project is Rs. 5221.23 Crore. The Scheme is scheduled to be 
implemented within 48 months from the date of investment approval. The project will facilitate 
drawal of power from other regions and its dispersal to various load centres of Western Region, 
including Maharashtra. It will also improve the reliability of the Western Region Grid.

records.title: FREQUENT TRAVELLER SCHEMES ON SHATABDI TRAINS .
details:

(SHRI R.VELU)
(a) & (b): With a view to improve the patronisation of higher classes, where occupancy level is relatively low as compared to that in Sleeper class and 3-AC classes, a Scheme of Frequent Travellers (SOFT) has been launched in the month of February, 2006, which is applicable to 1st AC, 2AC and AC Chair Car Classes. A Frequent Traveller will get a complimentary train trip after certain numbers of reward points are accumulated.

records.title: CONTINGENCY PLAN FOR CRUDE OIL PRICES
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI DINSHA PATEL)
(a): From the Energy Information Administration (EIA) reports and the latest Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) statements, it appears that international oil prices are expected to continue to remain high and even increase ha the near future, given the geopolitical pressures particularly in the Middle East region.
(b)to(d): In the context of unprecedented rise in international oil prices, the Government has taken a number of steps to protect the interest of common man. These include :-
 Policy of Equitable burden sharing mnongst three stakeholders namely, 
Government, PSU oil companies and the consmners.
Of the burden ofRs.73,500 crores, only 12% passed on to the consumers.

 LPG placed under declared goods restricting the states to charging just 
4% sales tax.
 Navaratna companies, have been made financially viable so they can, 
continue to serve the `commonman`.

records.title: CHEAPER DRUGS FOR AIDS .
details:
(a) the details of steps taken by Government to ensure availability of expensive drugs at lower prices to AIDS patients in the country; and
(b) the details of steps taken by Government to reduce the cost of HIV testing for lower-income people, comprising the high-risk groups in the country?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE 
(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)
(a) Anti-retroviral drugs used for treatment of AIDS are currently being given free of cost to nearly 35 thousand patients through 54 ART centres established in the country. 44 more ART centres are being set up during the current year to cover more patients for treatment of AIDS.
(b) Kits for diagnosis of HIV are being procured and supplied to states as commodity assistance. Nearly 60 lakh kits are being procured during 2006-07. These are made available at Integrated Counselling and Testing Centres, Antenatal Clinics, Blood Banks etc., for testing of HIV free of cost.

records.title: COMPREHENSIVE TRAUMA CARE ON NATIONAL HIGHWAYS .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
(SHRI K.H. MUNIYAPPA)
(a)to(c) Provision of assistance in case of road accident is basically the responsibility of the State Governments. The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare provides assistance to the States/ Union Territories (UTs) under the scheme of ‘Assistance for Capacity Building’ for upgradation of emergency services/trauma care facilities in hospitals including those located near the National Highways for the purpose of treatment of accident victims. 
This Ministry also provides ambulance to States/UTs to evacuate victims of accident to the nearest medical centre under National Highways Accident Relief Service Scheme (NHARSS). In addition, National Highways Authority of India deploys an ambulance at an average interval of 50 kms under their Operation and Maintenance Contracts/Build operates Transfer agreements on the completed stretches of National Highways entrusted to them.

records.title: LOW COST LOANS FOR RURAL HOUSING .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SURYAKANTA PATIL)
(a) According to the information made available by 2001 Census, 11.651 million 
households are living in unserviceable temporary houses in rural areas. 
(b) to (d) Under Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY), the Ministry of Rural Development is 
providing financial assistance amounting to Rs. 25,000/- per unit in plain areas and Rs. 
27,500/- in hilly/difficult areas, to the BPL rural poor for construction of a new dwelling 
unit or for replacement of an existing unserviceable temporary house. However, the 
District Rural Development Agencies (DRDAs) can utilize up to 20% of the total funds 
available under IAY, for up gradation of existing unserviceable temporary house or under 
Credit-cum-Subsidy Scheme for construction of a house with credit from banks/financial 
institutions. Rural households having an annual income of upto Rs. 32,000/- can avail of 
the facility under Credit-cum-Subsidy Scheme. Ceiling of subsidy under the scheme is 
Rs. 12,500/- per household and the balance amount has to be arranged by way of loan not 
exceeding Rs. 50,000/- in each case from banks/financial institutions.

records.title: PROMOTION OF HIGHER USE OF ETHANOL .
details:
Minister of State in the MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)
(a) to (c): With a view to reducing dependence on imported oil by way of encouraging use of indigenous sources of energy and to provide a supportive role to the sugarcane farmers, the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoP&NG) had introduced the scheme of mandatorily supplying 5% ethanol blended petrol in major sugar producing states and contiguous union territories w.e.f. 1.1.2003. However, the programme could be implemented only in a staggered manner because ethanol was not available in a consistent manner and at reasonable prices. MoP&NG issued an amending Notification dated 27.10.2004 making sale of EBP mandatory in 10 States and 3 UTs if the price of sourcing indigenous ethanol for supply of ethanol-blended petrol is comparable to the price of indigenous ethanol for alternative uses; the delivery price of ethanol at the locations is comparable to the import parity price of petrol at that location; and the indigenous ethanol industry is able to maintain uninterrupted supply of ethanol for ethanol-blended petrol programme at such prices.
 As regards procurement price of ethanol, the Public Sector Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have been procuring ethanol through public tenders. While the delivered price of petrol and ethanol at mixing depots would vary from location to location and from time to time, it is not correct to state that ethanol price may be a fraction of petrol price. In fact the availability of ethanol at reasonable prices has been one of the constraints in smooth implementation of the programme so far.

MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

records.title: CONGESTION IN MOBILE TELEPHONY .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)
(a) Congestion in the mobile telephony happens due to the problems within the network of the private mobile operators in addition to shortage of capacity at the points of interconnection among networks of telecom service providers including BSNL. Congestion is one of the reasons for poor quality of service from mobile phones. BSNL provides interconnection based on technical feasibility and as per the time frame provided in the interconnection agreement between BSNL and Private Operators.
(b) & (c) Interconnection provisioning is a continuous process. The Government has asked Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited and the private telecom operators to take various steps which inter-alia include holding of regular review meetings, streamlining of the procedure for provisioning of PoIs in time bound manner, to provide forecast for demand of PoIs in advance to enable BSNL to plan necessary equipment where feasible so as to reduce the cases of technical non-feasible.

records.title: ADDITION OF NUCLEAR ENERGY CAPACITY
details:
: 
(a) Whether it is a fact that Planning Commission has accepted a recommendation to raise India`s nuclear energy capacity to 100,000 MW in 25 years; and
(b) if so, the details of the proposal?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER`S OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN) : 
(a) The Planning Commission had constituted an expert committee to formulate
& an integrated energy policy for the country. The expert committee in its draft
(b) report has suggested the possibility of reaching a nuclear power capacity of 48000 MWe to 63000 MWe in the next 25 years or so, by a mix of indigenous Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors, Fast Breeder Reactors and Light Water Reactors based on imports and is contingent on availability of fuel/reactors through international cooperation in nuclear field.

records.title: SHORTFALL IN COLLECTION OF EDUCATION CESS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that the revenue receipts from the two per cent 
education cess in the first eight months of current fiscal at Rs. 2,400 
crore have been only a third of the budgeted yearly estimates of Rs. 6,975 
crore;
(b) whether Government are of the view that such drastic shortfall will have 
a negative impact on successful conduct of elementary and other education 
programmes like ‘Sarva Shiksha Abhiyaan’ ;
(c) if so, the details of any action contemplated to redress the shortfall 
of money; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?”

FINANCE MINISTER
 (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM)
(a) to (d) : A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a), (b), (c) and (d) OF RAJYA 
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.550 DUE FOR ANSWER ON 23-5-2006
(a): In the current fiscal, eight months have not yet been completed. 
However, during the last fiscal, so far as indirect taxes are concerned, 
Rs.2600.30 crore have been collected in the first eight months against the 
Budget Estimates (BE) of Rs.3572 crore which is 72.8% of the BE (of 
indirect taxes), much higher than the pro-rata target. Insofar as direct 
taxes are concerned, the information is not yet available for the last 
fiscal 2005-06. However, in the fiscal 2004-05, the education cess collected 
in respect of direct taxes was Rs.1804.51 crore (where as Rs.2514.22 crore 
was collected in respect of indirect taxes in 2004-05).
(b) to (d): No, Sir. Prarambhik Shiksha Kosh (PSK) has been shown as a 
separate line item in the Budget of 2006-07. Budget 2005-06 assumes 
Rs.6,975 crore as estimated receipts through “education cess”. The 
allocation made in BE 2005-06 for Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) and 
Mid-day-Meal (MDM) scheme was Rs.11,145.26 crore which was enhanced to Rs. 
11,156.01 crore in revised estimates of the fiscal 2005-06. The above 
allocations are irrespective of the fact whether revenue budgeted through 
education cess is actually realized or not.
In the current year also an amount of Rs.8,746 crore has been assumed 
as receipts through education cess, out of which Rs. 5831 crore has been 
allocated to SSA and Rs.2915 crore to MDM. As against this, the

details:
(a) whether Government propose to auction a large number of new oil and natural gas exploration blocks over the next two years
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the total estimated yield of crude oil and gas respectively from these blocks?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI DINSHA PATEL)
(a) to (c):- With a view to attract private investment including foreign investment for exploration and exploitation of Hydrocarbon resources in the 26 sedimentary basins of the country covering onland and offshore areas, the Government has been inviting bids from private companies on a regular basis since, 1991. To give further impetus to the exploration efforts, the Government has formulated the New exploration Licensing Policy ( NELP) which provides equal opportunities and a level playing field to foreign companies and Indian companies, both Public Sector Undertakings ( PSUs) and private companies to bid for exploration acreages, offered by the Government from time to time. Exploration activities including identification and offer of blocks through NELP is a continuous and ongoing process. The Government of India, on 23rd February, 2006, has offered 55 blocks comprising of 24 deep water, 6 shallow water and 25 onshore blocks under the sixth round of New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP-VI). The bid closing date for these blocks is 15th September, 2006. These are exploration blocks where exploration of oil and gas is proposed to be carried out. The exploration period for these blocks is 7-8 years. Being exploration blocks, oil and gas reserves have to be established through exploration, hence any estimation of reserves would be pre-mature.

details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE 
(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)
(a) to (d) : There are various mechanisms by which quality of services and care provided by hospitals and other health care institutions can be assessed. Some of these are Accreditation, Certification and Rating. Concerned health institutions obtain these quality benchmarks depending on their own requirement and the requirement of clients they serve. Government of India is of the view that Accreditation etc. is to be purely a voluntary process and, therefore, should be left to independent specialist agencies outside the Government set up. There can also be more than one agency that could undertake such accreditation, certification or rating. Such agencies will fix their own standards. The Quality Council of India, which is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, has set up a National Accreditation Board of Hospital (NABH).
 The purpose of accreditation/rating is to assure the patients about the quality of services available in the accredited hospital.

details:

(d) the details of action taken or proposed to be taken by
 Government to improve the water distribution across the
 country?

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES 
(PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ)
(a) The Ministry of Urban Development have reported that no
complaint has been received by them from any of the State
Government/ Urban Local Bodies (ULB) regarding large scale
corruption and irregularities in distribution of potable water in
cities across the country.
(b) & (c) As per report on study titled “Status of Water supply and
Sanitation and Solid Waste Management in Urban areas” conducted by
National Institute of Urban Affairs, New Delhi under the sponsorship
of Ministry of Urban Development, the unaccounted for water (UFW)
mainly in Indian cities is of the order of 40-50%, while acceptable
value according to Central Public Health Engineering and Environment
Organisation’s norms is 15%.
(d) The Ministry of Urban Development have launched a new programme
namely, “Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission” (JNNURM)
with an aim to encourage reforms and fast track planned development
of identified cities. The focus is to be on efficiency in urban
infrastructure (water supply) service delivery mechanism, community
participation and accountability of ULBs. The JNNURM envisages
various mandatory and obligatory reform measures. One of the
mandatory reforms to be carried out by the ULBs is “Levy of
reasonable user charges by ULB/Parastatals with the objective that
full cost of operation and maintenance or recurring cost is
collected within next seven years. However, cities/towns in North
East and other special category States may recover atleast 50% of
operation and maintenance charges initially. These cities/towns
should graduate to full O&M cost recovery in a phased manner”.

records.title: (clubbed) STRENGTHENING OF SPECIAL TASK FORCE DEALING WITH NAXALISM .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether the review meeting of the coordination centre on Naxalism was held in April, 2006 
to discuss strengthening of the special task force both in terms of manpower and response time and extreme violence in 13 States, high profile attacks, detaining of train in Jharkhand, blasting truck in Chhattisgarh and jail break in Orissa;
(b) whether the PM also called a meeting of 13 Naxal affected States on the 13th April, 2006; and
(c) if so, what were the main decisions taken to check the Naxal menace in those States?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )
(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to Rajya Sabha Starred Question No. 375 for 10.5.2006 regarding “Strengthening of special task force dealing with Naxalism”.
(a) & (b): The 2nd meeting of the Standing Committee of the Chief Ministers of the naxal affected States and the Coordination Centre meeting were held in New Delhi on 13.4.2006 and 31.3.2006, respectively to comprehensively review the naxal situation in the affected states and consider appropriate strategies and measures to deal with the problem.
(c): The main decisions of the above meetings are annexed.
ANNEXURE
MAJOR DECISIONS OF THE 2ND MEETING OF THE STANDING COMMITTEE OF THE CHIEF MINISTERS OF NAXAL AFFECTED STATES AND 20TH MEETING OF THE COORDINATION CENTRE:
(i) The States will prepare/revise and implement comprehensive 
but realistic action plans at the State and district levels with short-term and 
long-term approaches and strategies to combat the naxalite menace 
simultaneously on political, security and development fronts.
(ii) The States will strengthen and improve ground level 
policing and initiate action to fill up vacancies particularly in the police 
stations in the naxal affected areas on utmost priority and such police 
stations will be fortified in a time bound manner by utilizing funds under the 
Police Modernization (PM) Scheme.
(iii) The State Governments and RPF will take steps to put in 
place effective coordination on ground between RPF, GRP, local police and 
intelligence agencies to ensure protection and safety of railway passengers, 
trains and other railway infrastructure.
(iv) The States will consider and take steps to constitute Joint 
Task Forces of neighbouring States to enhance the effectiveness of intelligence 
driven inter-State joint operations against naxalites and their infrastructure.
(v) The States will give higher priority and focused attention 
on socio-economic development in the naxal affected areas through convergence 
of existing developmental schemes and fund missing links, if any, in these 
schemes by utilizing funds under BDI etc.
(vi) The States will take immediate policy and operational 
measures for speedy and effective implementation of land reforms, putting in 
place a progressive and forward looking rehabilitation and resettlement policy 
for displaced tribals, ensuring meaningful implementation of PESA 
withdrawing/compounding of minor forest offences and allowing debt waiver in 
the naxal affected areas. 
(vii) The States will post young and committed officers in both 
civil and police administration with a stable tenure in naxal affected 
districts to effectively address security and development issues in these 
areas.
(viii) The Central Government will continue to provide all 
possible help to the States on both security and development fronts to enable 
them to successfully meet the challenge posed by naxalism.

records.title: DEVELOPMENT OF SICK SSIS NO
details:
(a): whether Government are aware of recent RBI report stating
 that increasing incidences of SSIs declaring themselves sick is a
 reason for slowing growth of flow of bank credit to the sector;
(b): whether Government are of the view that the trend may lead
 to drying up of a major source of financial assistance to the 
 SSIs in the country; and 
(c): whether any plans have been formulated or steps being taken
 to increase and promote the credit and loan sources for
 development of SSI sector in India?
 ANSWER 
 (SHRI MAHABIR PRASAD)

MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES & AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES 
(a)to(c): A statement is placed on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO. 318 FOR ANSWER ON 13.03.2006 RAISED BY SHRI
RAJEEV SHUKLA.
(a): According to information received from the Reserve Bank of
India (RBI), it has not brought out any report recently which
mentions that incidences of small scale industries (SSIs) 
declaring themselves sick is increasing or the credit flow to this
sector from banks is slowing down. On the contrary, according to
the information provided by the RBI, the number of sick SSIs has
declined from 1,67,980 as at the end of March 2003 to 1,38,041 as
the end of March 2005. During the same period, the loans from the
public sector banks outstanding against the SSI has gone up from 
Rs. 52,988 crore to Rs. 67,634 crore.
(b)&(c): In view of the declining trend in sickness and increasing
trend in flow of credit to the SSI as stated in reply to part (a) 
above, there is no question of the bank finance to the SSI drying 
up. On the contrary, the `Policy Package for Stepping up Credit to
Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)` as announced by the Central 
Government on 10th August, 2005 envisages a minimum of 20 per cent 
year-on-year growth in credit to the SME sector, leading to 
doubling of the loan outstanding in a period of 5 years. Based on
this Policy Package, the RBI has already issued detailed
guidelines to the public sector banks on 19th August, 2005.
This Package also includes some other measures to increase 
quantum of credit to SMEs (including SSI), such as 
(i) public 
sector banks to follow a transparent rating system with cost of
credit linked to the credit rating of the enterprise, 
(ii) 
commercial banks to make concerted efforts to provide credit cover
on an average to at least 5 new tiny, small and medium enterprises 
at each of their semi-urban/urban branches per year, 
(iii) special
dispensation under the Credit Guarantee Scheme for all (a) loans 
upto Rs. 2 lakh, (b) eligible women entrepreneurs and (c) eligible 
borrowers located in the North Eastern region (including Sikkim) 
and Jammu and Kashmir, 
(iv) adoption of cluster-based approach by 
banks for SME financing, etc.

records.title: DIETARY SUPPLEMENTS AND MEDICAL DEVICES UNDER DRUGS AND COSMETICS ACT .
details:
(a) whether Government have received any suggestionS to bring dietary supplementS and medical devices under the purview of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, for effective monitoring of their quality and prices;
(b) if so, the details of any action taken by Government in this regard?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE 
(SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)
(a) & (b) The report of the Expert Committee on Comprehensive Examination of Drug Regulatory Issues, including the Problem of Spurious Drugs (Mashelkar Committee), had recommended that there is need to have separate regulation defining dietary supplements, laying criteria of permissible limit of ingredients and a procedure of evaluation of safety and efficacy, information to consumers and provision related to their advertisements. It was also recommended that these products should be regulated under PFA or any other emergent mechanism/infrastructure. Products that claim or are intended to diagnose, cure, prevent or treat a disease are to be classified as drugs as is the current rule. (para 7.11 to 7.1.19 of the said report) Central Committee on food standards (CCFS) has recommended that productS marketed as dietary supplements belonging to certain specified categories need to be considered under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules. 
As regards medical devices, the suggestion of Mashelkar Committee was to specifically define them under Section 3 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and to create a specific medical devices division for their regulation. The Committee has also recommended for an appropriate regulatory mechanism to be set up under Central Drug Authority for certification, quality assurance and post marketing surveillance of imported as well as locally made medical devices. A Committee under DDG(M) has been to go into these recommendations and suggest appropriate legislation. In the mean time 10 sterile medical devices which are of critical nature, have been notified. By the Government under Section 3(b)
(iv) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act in order to ensure appropriate regulation over their import and manufacture.

records.title: BENEFITS TO FARMERS FROM RISING MARKET PRICES .
details:
MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. 181 FOR 03/03/2006 REGARDING BENEFITS TO FARMERS FROM 
RISING MARKET PRICES.
(a) to (d): Marketing of wheat along with other notified commodities is regulated under the Agricultural Produce Marketing Regulation Act (APMC Act). The whole geographical area in the State is divided asmarket area wherein markets are managed by the Market Committees. As a consequence of such a regulation, the farmer is restricted from entering into direct contract with any bulk buyer, as the produce is required to be canalized through regulated markets. The monopoly of the regulated market has enabled the intermediaries operating therein to take a disproportionate share of the price paid by the consumer. As per the available information, the producer`s share in the consumer`s price in major wheat producing States varied between 
71.1% to 85.72%. The balance is accounted for by charges such as mandi charges, sales tax, weighing charges, palledari, brokerage, transport cost and market margins.
 Government has taken several steps to ensure that the farmers get adequate benefit from the higher market price for their crops. These are as follows:-
(i) This Ministry is proactively encouraging the State Governments to 
promote new competitive 
markets in private and cooperative sectors and allow direct marketing and 
contract farming 
programmes by suitably amending APMC Act. This is with the objective of 
promoting fair 
competition, so that the farmers can gain from the options available, and take 
their produce to the centres that offer the best prices/services including 
regulated markets.
(ii) This Ministry is implementing a capital investment subsidy scheme 
titled `Construction of Rural Godowns` w.e.f. 01.04.2001, to provide the 
farming community with facilities for scientific 
storage so that wastage and produce deterioration are avoided and also to 
enable it to meet its 
credit requirement without being compelled to sell the produce at a time when 
the prices are low. 
The scheme has been made farmer friendly by allowing subsidy for smaller 
godowns of 50 MT 
size in general and of 25 MT in hilly areas. Five lakh tonnes capacity to be 
created is reserved for small farmers. Till 31.12.2005, 10932 storage projects 
having a capacity of 158.68 lakh tonne have been sanctioned under the scheme by 
providing a subsidy of Rs.279.91 crore.
(iii) Government has permitted futures trading in wheat at the commodity 
exchange to enable farmer to disover prices of traded commodities including 
wheat well in advance of the crop season thus enabling them to decide when to 
sell his produce.
(iv) In addition, to ensure payment of remunerative prices to the 
farmers, the Government announces Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for major 
crops. The price support mechanism enables the 
farmers to sell their produce at remunerative prices, whenever the market 
prices tend to fall below the MSP level.

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
(DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH)
(a),(b)&(c): At present the Central Government makes available wheat, rice, sugar and K. Oil under the Public Distribution System to the State Government for distribution through the Fair Price Shops (FPS). In order to increase the viability of FPSs, under the System, the State Governments have been advised to allow the FPSs, to deal with other items of daily consumption/use also.  FPSs have also been allowed to be used as STD booths.

details:

(a): The foodgrain production in the country shows an upward trend albeit with year to year 
fluctuations. The total production of foodgrains in 1995-96 was 180.42 million tonnes which 
increased over the years to `reach 213.46 million` tonnes` in 2003-04. In 2004-05 `as `per` the

(b): The International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) in its report titled `2020 Global Food Outlook` mentioned that India would shift from near self-sufficiency under the baseline scenario (Scenario prevailing in and around 1997) to imports of 30 million (tonnes of cereals).
(c) to (e): As per National Agriculture Policy, special efforts are made to raise the productivity and production of crops to meet the increasing demand for food generated by demographic pressures and raw materials for expanding agro-based industries. details:

status so far?

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES 
(PROF. SAIF-UD-DIN SOZ)
(a) & (b) The Ministry of Water Resources (MOWR) and Central
Water Commission (CWC) formulated a National Perspective
Plan (NPP) for Water Resources Development in 1980
envisaging interbasin transfer of water from surplus basins
to deficit ones. NPP comprises of two components,viz 
(i)
Himalayan rivers development component and 
(ii) Peninsular
rivers development component. National Water Development
Agency (NWDA) was set up in 1982 as a registered Society
under MOWR to carry out detailed studies for NPP. NWDA,
based on water balance and other studies, identified 30
links (14 under Himalayan and 16 under Peninsular) for

policy, irrigation projects are planned, investigated,
formulated, implemented and funded by the State governments
out of their own resources and as per their own priorities.
Therefore, the works to resolve irregularities of water
distribution are carried out by State Governments and the
Central Government does not contemplate smaller links
between rivers and canals.

records.title: VACANT POSTS OF JUDGES IN HIGH COURTS .
details:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H. R. BHARDWAJ)
(a), (b), (c) & (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
Statement referred to in reply to parts (a), (b), (c) & (d) of the Rajya Sabha Starred Question
No. 34 for answer on 20.2.2006.
Against the sanctioned strength Of 675 Judges in 21 High Courts, 553 Judges were in position as on 15.2.2006, leaving 122 vacancies to be filled up.2. Filling up of vacancies in the High Courts is a continuous consultative process among the constitutional authorities. While every effort is made to fill up the existing vacancies expeditiously, vacancies`do keep arising on account of retirements, resignation or elevation of Judges.
3. After the Supreme Court Judgment of October 6, 1993 in the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record & Ant. Vs. Union of India, read with the Advisory Opinion of October 28, i998, the entire process of initiation of proposal for appointment of a Judge of a High Court lies with the Chief Justice of that High Court. Government has been periodically reminding the Chief Justices of the High Courts and the Chief Ministers of the States to initiate proposals for filling up all vacant posts of judges in the High Courts as also those which will be falling vacant during the next six months.
4. The judge strength of the High Courts is reviewed every three
years. For review of Judge strength, the average institution and the pendency of main cases during the last five years is considered by taking into account the national average or the average rate of disposal of main cases per Judge per year in that ttigh Court, whichever is higher. If the disposal per Judge in the concerned High Court is below even the national average then instead of increasing the strength, the concerned High Court is required to take steps for improvement in the rate of disposal of cases. If the average disposal of concerned High Court is above the national average then increase in Judge strength is accordingly considered. The strength of Additional Judges is` reviewed only if there is an increase in the arrears of the pending cases during the last 5 years and the disposal per Judge is above the national average. The last review was undertaken in the year 2003 when 94 new posts were recommended. As an interim review, 4 posts of Judges were approved for the Bombay High Court in 2005, making the total for increase of 98 posts. The next review is due in 2006 for which the High Courts have been requested to furnish data.

records.title: INEQUALITIES IN HEALTHCARE DELIVERY SYSTEM .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE 
( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)
(a) & (b) The National Health Policy, 2002 has given over riding importance to ensuring more equitable access to health services across the country. As health is a State subject, the policy has emphasised that the State Governments would need to design specific schemes wherever required, to suit the health needs of their region.
The Government of India is implementing National Health Programmes for control of major communicable and non communicable diseases like Malaria, TB, Leprosy, AIDS, blindness, cancer 
and mental health which cover the entire country. With a view to removing regional imbalances and availability of tertiary health facilities, six AIIMS like institutions are to be set up in the under served areas of the country and several institutions are to be upgraded to that level. Recently the Government has launched a National Rural Health Mission to provide accessible, affordable, accountable, effective and reliable primary health care especially to the poor and vulnerable sections of the population. It has as its key components provision of a female 
health activist in each village in select states a village health plan prepared through a local team headed by the Health and Sanitation committee of the Panchayat; strengthening of the rural hospital for effective curative care and made measurable and accountable to the community through Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS); and integration of vertical Health and Family Welfare Programmes and Funds for optimal utilization of funds and infrastructure and strengthening delivery of primary health care.
(c) & (d) The National Health Policy, 2002 welcomes the participation of the private sector in all the areas of health activities - Primary, Secondary and Tertiary - with suitable regulatory mechanisms. The private sector increasingly is participating in the delivery of health care particularly in National Programmes like TB, Blindness, HIV/AIDS, amongst others. The Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) also engages some private hospitals for providing treatment to the CGHS beneficiaries. Health is a State subject. Public Private Partnership is also an important strategy under NRHM.

shift entire business process of Registrar of Companies to e-governance mode; and 
(b) if so, the details of the proposals alongwith status of its implementation?

THE MINISTER OF COMPANY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI PREM CHAND GUPTA) 
(a) Yes, Sir.
(b) The Ministry of Company Affairs (MCA) has launched an ambitious e-Governance and modernization programme called `MCA21 e-Governance Project` on 01.03.2005. The Project aims at transforming MCA into a paperless, modern, service-oriented, quality conscious and customer centric organization, envisages shifting entire business process of Registrar of Companies to e-governance mode. After implementation, all services, such as registration of new companies, filing of annual returns and balance sheets, filing of event based documents and also viewing
of documents etc. will be available to public online through Internet. 
The Project envisages:
- Digitisation of legacy data of Companies and Annual Returns & Balance Sheets 
of two years running into approx. 6.0 crore pages.
- Setting-up of facilitation centers at 53 locations throughout the country. 
These are known as Physical Front Offices (PFOs) and will remain operational 
for a period of three years.
 As per plan, the Project is to be implemented within a period of 60 weeks 
starting 1.3.2005. The Project implementation will start as pilots from mid 
January in phases leading to nation-wide rollout by the end of April, 2006. The 
implementation is going ahead as per schedule.

records.title: CROP HARVESTING LOSSES .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that crop harvesting losses in India are as huge as
 Rs.65,000 crores per year;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) the details of steps being contemplated by Government to control and minimize 
 harvesting losses of such a magnitude?

MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)
(a)&(b): In a study conducted by the Directorate of Marketing & Inspection post harvest losses at producers` level have been estimated to be varying from 1.79 to 7.14 per cent for foodgrains and pulses and from 16.35 to 30.00 per cent in the case of fruits and vegetables. The wastage depends on nature of produce, its shelf life, mode of transportation, packaging, processing, distance from the market, availability of infrastructure facilities like rural godowns and cold storage etc.
(c): The Government has taken the following step to reduce post-harvest losses in the country.
 Indian Council of Agricultural Research has been developing new techniques/systems to minimize the losses in agricultural produce in the country through the Central Institute of Post Harvest Engineering & Technology, Ludhiana and the all India Coordinated Research Project on Post Harvest Technology. The All India Coordinated Research Project on Post Harvest Technology has 33 co-operative centres located throughout the country to develop regionally differentiated post harvest technology packages for crop, livestock product and fisheries produce in terms of reducing post harvest losses, aiding value to the main produce and 
by-products.
 National Horticulture Board, an autonomous body under this Ministry is implementing programmes to reduce post harvest losses by providing investment subsidy on the capital cost of infrastructure projects for post-harvest handling, processing and marketing of horticulture produce. The rate of subsidy is 20 percent of the project cost with a maximum limit of Rs.25 lakh per project. 
 The Department is also implementing schemes for construction/modernization of Cold Storage and Rural godowns in the country with a view to provide scientific storage facilities to farmers. Under these schemes, subsidy is provided @ 25% of capital cost of the storage project in general and @ 33.33 percent in case of North Eastern States, hilly areas and Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes entrepreneurs. The scheme of Construction of Rural Godown has recently been revised to restrict subsidy on the storage projects for individual, companies and corporations @ 15 percent of the project cost.

records.title: . INSTITUTIONALIZATION OF ARBITRATION .
details:
MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
(SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ)
(a) & (b): Yes, Sir. The Departmental Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Personnel, Public Grievances, Law & Justice which examined the Arbitration and
Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2003 introduced in Rajya Sabha on 22na December,
2003 in its Ninth Report presented to Rajya Sabha on 4th August, 2005 recommended a
legislation incorporating provisions relating to institutionalised arbitration. The
Committee felt that intitutionalised arbitration would end the alleged unethical practice
followed by some institutions as at present. This will also bring in accountability of
arbitrators and committed people to conclude the arbitration proceedings in a time
bound manner failing which there could be penalty for delay in settlement of disputes.
(c), (d) & (e): Yes, Sir. Institutionalised arbitration will bring in fully dedicated panel of
lawyers and arbitrators devoting full time for arbitration proceedings. It will also
considerably reduce delay in settlement of disputes occurring at present due to
availability of arbitrators and arbitration lawyers only on a part time basis. The
Government considers that mediation, conciliation, fast tract courts, lok adalats, etc,
would also pave way for early resolution of disputes besides institutionalised arbitration
proceedings.

 such infiltration?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
( SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL )
(a): As per the report of the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir,
infiltration across the border in the State increased in May 2005 as compared 
to the previous months of this year. Level of infiltration declined in the 
month of June but it increased again in July. However, overall level of 
terrorist infiltration in the State has come down significantly this year till 
July 31, as compared to the corresponding period last year.
(b): Details are given below:-
2005 Estimated no. of Infiltrators 
May 43
June 21
July 67
(c): The Government, jointly with the State Government, have 
adopted a multi-pronged approach, to contain cross-border infiltration in Jammu 
and Kashmir, which includes, inter-alia, strengthening of border management and 
multi-tiered and multi-modal deployment along International Border/Line of 
Control and near the ever changing infiltration routes, construction of border 
fencing, improved technology, weapons and equipment for security forces, 
improved intelligence and operational coordination and synergising intelligence 
flow to check infiltration and pro-active action against the terrorists within 
the State. The counter infiltration efforts are reviewed periodically at 
various levels in the State Government (including the two Unified Headquarters 
headed by the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir) and in the Central 
Government.

records.title: USE OF KEROSENE FOR ADULTERATION .
details:
MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS & PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR)
(a) & (b): The Government have commissioned the first-ever detailed study of Kerosene demand 
in the country, through the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) in December 
2004. They have submitted their interim report in June 2005. While, the interim report does not
indicate the extent of pilferage of PDS kerosene, the final report is likely to attempt an 
estimate the diversion of PDS kerosene for unintended usage. As per the interim report, nearly
73% of households in rural areas use kerosene for lighting purposes.
(c) : The total cost of kerosene imported during 2002-03, 2003-04 and 2004-05 was about Rs.808
crore, Rs.890 crore and Rs.429 crore respectively.
(d) : In order to check pilferage and misuse of kerosene and to ensure that highly subsidized
kerosene supplied under the Public Distribution Network (PDS) reaches the targeted consumers,
the Government have developed an innovative scheme for the marketing of PDS kerosene called “
Jan Kerosene Pariyojana”. The scheme would be initially implemented as a pilot project w.e.f. 
2.10.2005 covering about 10% of the blocks in the country. Based on the experience of the pilot
project and its evaluation by an independent agency, the scheme would be further extended to 
cover all the blocks in the country.
(e) : In order to promote use of LPG in rural households, Government have directed Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs) to concentrate on setting up more distributorships in rural areas 
and also to adopt innovative methods such as sale through rural mobile vehicles, setting up 
community kitchens, and sale of small size 5 kg. Cylinders for low income group customers.

records.title: EFFECT OF CECA WITH SINGAPORE ON INDIAN PRIVATE BANKS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that recently approved Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA) with Singapore has provisions that confer exclusive privileges to banks based out of Singapore, including option of merging with or acquiring Indian private Banks;
(b) if so, whether the said provision can have far-reaching, negative consequences for the
 Indian banking industry; and
(c) whether Government will make suitable alterations to the provisions of CECA to protect interests of Indian private banks?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
(SHRI E.V.K.S. ELANGOVAN )
(a) to (c): Under the recently approved India-Singapore Comprehensive 
Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA), Singapore Banks are permitted to invest 
in private sector banks in India through the FDI route subject to the following 
conditions :-
- Total foreign investment (both FDI and FII) should not exceed 74%.
- Banks will have to follow the one mode of presence criteria laid down by RBI. 
Under this criteria, foreign banks can have a presence in the Indian markets 
through one of these forms ; (a) branches (b) not more than one wholly owned 
subsidiaries (c) Joint ventures.

details:
(a) whether it is a fact that civil courts in lower Judiciary combined with High Courts and Supreme Court are the only constitutional institutions to observe summer and winter vacations;
(b) whether it is also a fact that hundreds of thousands of court cases are pending and that theirnumber shows no signs of abating;
(c) whether in view of 
(a) and 
(b) above, Government would consider to put an end to the
colonial practice of courts observing summer vacations; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW & JUSTICE 
(SHRI K.VENKATAPATHY)
(a) to (d); The working days in the Supreme Court and High Courts are regulated by the rules framed by the respective Courts, According to available information, the Supreme Court of India works for 222 days in a year; all High Courts in the country normally have 210 working days in a year and the number of working days of the District/Subordinate Courts are regulated by the concerned High Court.
The question of curtailing/discontinuing the vacations in the Courts has been considered in the past, but it has not been found feasible or advisable to do so because of the taxing nature of work of the Judiciary and the Bar. The Department of Justice in July 2001 had invited the views of the High .Courts regarding the number of working days in the High Courts and the curtailment of their vacations. Replies were received from 14 High Courts. The High Court of Uttaranchal increased the number of its working days in a year from 210 to 224 and the High Court of Karnataka from 210 to 214. Jharkhand High Court had no objection to increase the number of working days. Other High Courts had not favoured increase in the number of their working days in a year.
In view of the urgent need of the hour to reduce the huge pendencies prevailing in the High Courts, this Department addressed to all the High Courts, requesting them to fix the period of vacations in such a way that the number of working days of High Courts generally do not fall below 222 days in a year.
Various other steps have been taken by the Government to expedite disposal of cases, these include periodically monitoring the pendency position in courts, grouping of cases involving common question of law, constitution of specialized benches, timely filling up the vacancies of judges, increasing the judge strength, organizing Lok Adalats at regular intervals, encouraging alternative modes of disputes resolution like negotiation, mediation and arbitration and setting up of special tribunals like Central Administrative Tribunals, State Administrative Tribunals, Income Tax Appellate Tribunals, Family Courts, Labour Courts etc,

records.title: FACILITIES TO PREGNANT WORKING WOMEN .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY
OF HEALTH & FAMILY WELFARE 
( SMT. PANABAKA LAKSHMI)
(a) to (d): Several laws have been enacted to secure reasonable working conditions for women workers and to prevent their exploitation. Special provisions have been made under various labour laws to provide facilities to pregnant working women. Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, maternity benefits are to be provided on completion of 80 days working. No work of arduous nature, long hours of standing likely to interfere with pregnancy/normal development of foetus which may cause miscarriage or is likely to affect health. On production of medical certificate, advance maternity benefit as per law is to be allowed. Rs.250 as Medical bonus to be given when no prenatal confinement and post-natal care is provided free of charge.
The insured women covered under ESI Act are provided medical care by way of Pre-natal Care (ante-natal care including immunisation & prophylaxes against iron deficiency anaemia). Natal care (all services related to delivery of child) and Post-Natal Care (regular check-ups, counselling for family welfare and immunisation of child) and maternity benefits by way of cash benefits for all days on which she does not work for remuneration during a period of 12 weeks for confinement, 6 weeks in case of miscarriage and additional one month in case of sickness arising out of pregnancy, confinement, pre-mature birth of child or miscarriage or medical termination of pregnancy as per provisions of Section 56 & 50 of ESI Act, 1948 and Regulations thereof. No separate specific policy for Nursing working mothers is available in ESI Act, 1948.
Under the Plantation Labour Act, 1951, women workers are provided time off for feeding children. 
Under the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996, provisions for maternity benefit to female beneficiaries of the Welfare Fund have been made.

records.title: SHORTFALL OF POWER DURING ENSUING SUMMER .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that the extent of power shortfall in the country is expected to grow 
hugely in the coming summer months when demand peaks;
(b) if so, whether Government is planning any steps to manage this shortfall and ensure 
uninterrupted supplies; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )
(a) : Energy shortage in the country during the summer months (April – July, 2005) is 
anticipated to be of the order of 4% of the total energy requirement of the country as compared 
to 6% during the same period last year.
(b) & (c) : The following measures are being taken to augment availability of power in the 
country during ensuing summer months:
(i) Export of power from surplus regions to deficit regions. 
(ii) Load management:-Imposition of statutory power cuts/restriction and load 
 shedding by State Government/Power Utilities from time to time depending upon the 
 availability of power.
(iii) Coordinated operation and maintenance of hydro/thermal/nuclear gas turbine power 
 station in the regional power system to optimally utilize the existing generation capacity.
(iv) Installation of shunt capacitors to improve voltage profiles of regional grids.
(v) Import of coal to bridge the gap between demand and availability of domestic coal and 
 consequently enhance generation from coal based power stations.

records.title: STEM CELL RESEACH .
details:
(a) 
(a) whether Government feel a need for regulating stem-cell research in India;
(b) 
(b) if so, the details of any legislation being considered in this behalf; and
(c) 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER OF
STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT
(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL) 
(a), (b) &(c) Yes Sir,
National Bioethics Committee set up by the Department of Biotechnology(DBT) with the approval of Hon`ble Minister of Science and Technology, in its sixth meeting recommended promotion of stem cell research in the country in view of its vast potential and its clinical use. There are no special legal or ethical problems in respect to stem cells, derived from adults, bone marrows or foetal cord blood. However, in respect to embryonic stem cells the Government does not allow generation of embryos for the sole purpose of obtaining stem cells. Only surplus or spare or supernumerary embryos can be used with the permission of couples from registered Assisted Reproductive Technique (ART) clinics.
The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare was requested by the Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI) to prepare appropriate guidelines to help in regulation of stem cell research and its application. Accordingly, a drafting committee provided brief guidelines for regulatory aspects of stem cell research to DCGI. These draft guidelines have been put on the website of the ICMR. The guidelines suggested constituting a multidisciplinary National Apex Committee (NAC) to monitor stem cell research activities in the country. It was also emphasized that newer technology should be thoroughly examined before approving any research. It was further suggested that this committee should examine all proposals involving stem cells of any source. Centres involved in stem cell research should be
registered with the committee. Currently in the absence of a National Committee, an Expert Committee has been constituted to monitor and review stem cell research activities under ICMR.
The issues regarding legislation and ethical issues involved in stem cell research are being discussed by a joint working group of ICMR and DBT.

records.title: EARLY WARNING SYSTEM FOR TSUNAMI .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY AND MINISTER 
OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAPIL SIBAL)
(a) Yes, Sir. It is proposed to set up a `tsunami and storm surges warning system` in the 
country with the following components:
 Strengthening of the existing seismological network to identify in near real time 
occurrence of a tsunamigenic earthquake.
 Installation of tsunami warning sensors close to the ocean bottom at appropriate
locales in the Indian Ocean, with real time connectivity.
 Tide gauge and data buoys networking.
 Modeling of the inundation scenarios for the entire coast.
= The establishment of a centre for collection of the information,.`analysis and 
generating Tsunami and Storm Surge advisories
(b) No, Sir. After such a system is in place and warning systems are made near real time 
then networking with countries in the Indian Ocean who might require prior information in 
case of a Tsunami would be done for exchange of information for their
benefit and mutual benefit.
(c) & (d): The system would cost about Rs.125 crores. India will bear this cost. The work
has been initiated. Different components would be achieved with passage of time and the 
system will be fully operational by September 2007.

records.title: AIR POLLUTION .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS 
(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA)
(a)&(b) A decreasing trend has been observed in the Sulphur-dioxide (SO²) levels in residential areas of many major cities. The trend in annual average concentration of Nitrogen-dioxide (NO2) is fluctuating in most of the cities and levels of Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM) are usually higher than the stipulated standards mainly due to natural dusty conditions. 
(c) Based on the ambient air quality monitored under the National Ambient Air Quality Programme (NAAQM), Central Pollution Control Board, in coordination with the State Pollution Control Boards, has identified top ten cities on the basis of RSPM levels observed in the residential areas during 2003 ( a list enclosed.) A similar trend of air pollution is observed (n these ten c/ties as that of ma)or cities stated above. 
(d) The Government has taken various steps to check air pollution levels within safe thresholds in the worst affected cities, which include -
 Notification of general and source specific emission standards.
- Enforcement of auto exhaust emission standards for new vehicles at
 manufacturing stage.
- Improved fuel quality.
 Use of beneficiated coal in the thermal power stations.
 Regular monitoring for compliance of environmental standards in 17
 categories of industries. Legal action is taken in case of defaulting units.
- A road map up to 2010 has been developed to control vehicular
 pollution for both the new and in-use vehicles.
 New emission norms for in-use vehicles have been introduced from
 October, 2004.

records.title: UTILISATION OF FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESERVES .
details:
(a) Whether Government are aware of the reports in the media
 on differences of opinion between the Reserve Bank of India 
and his Ministry in the matter of utilization of part of 
foreign exchange reserves for development of infrastructure ; 
(b) Whether in view of the larger requirement of funds for 
the purpose, how do Government propose to raise funds, 
particularly since RBI is not in favour of utilizing the
 forex reserves for the purpose;
(c) Whether regulatory agencies are being contemplated to
 be set up in the Planning Commission to make infrastructure
 funding by the private sector more attractive; and 
(d) If so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(Shri S.S. Palanimanickam)
a): India`s total foreign exchange reserves are now 
more than US$128 billion. Any decision to utilise a 
part of these reserves for funding domestic projects
requires a careful assessment, inter alia, of the impact 
of such a measure on the fiscal situation, money supply,
exchange rate, domestic interest rates, reserve adequacy
and inflation. An informed debate on the feasibility of 
such an utilisation is currently on. 
(b): The latest Union Budget (2004-05) has underlined 
enhancing investment - both public and private - in 
industry, as a thrust area, and has reiterated the
commitment to remove inadequacies in infrastructural
facilities. Specific measures aiming to enhance 
investment like increasing foreign direct investment 
(FDI) ceiling in civil aviation, and setting up an 
Investment Commission for inviting domestic and foreign
businesses to invest in India, have already been taken. 
(c) : No, Sir. 
(d) : Does not arise.
