records.title: (clubbed) SUICIDE BY FARMERS IN KARNATAKA .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) the number of farmers who committed suicide in Karnataka since 1998;
(b) the measures taken by Government to prevent such deaths and the number of families paid 
compensation and the amount of compensation, so paid;
(c) the special incentives announced by Hon`ble Prime Minister for the farmers of Andhra 
Pradesh and when the same incentives would be extended to farmers of Karnataka; and if not, the 
reasons therefor; and
(d) whether Government have announced any fresh package for the welfare of farmers?

MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI SHARAD PAWAR)
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED 
QUESTION NO. 148 FOR 10/12/2004 REGARDING SUICIDE BY FARMERS IN 
KARNATAKA.
(a): According to information received from the Government of Karnataka the number of farmers 
who have committed suicide in the State since 1998 is as follows:-
S.No. Year Figures of State Crime Records Bureau Figures of 
Agriculture Department 
1. 1998-99 2039 
2. 1999-2000 2379 - 
3. 2000-01 2630 
4. 2001-02 2505 
5. 2002-03 2340 
6. 2003-04 708
(b): The State Government has announced a series of measures for the farming community to tide 
over the situation. With a view to providing relief to the farmers and for revival of agricultural 
operations, Government of Karnataka announced a relief package comprising the following: -
? Waiver of interest on co-operative short-term loans for Rabi-2002. No penal interest 
on short-term agricultural loans by cooperatives in future. Rebate on current interest 
for long-term loans to the farmers at the rate of 5.5% to be reimbursed by the 
Government provided the farmers pay the remaining interest on 9%. 
? To write off outstanding loan and interest on failed wells.
? Full waiver of the outstanding dues to the State Electricity Board from the farmers as 
on 31.3.2001 in respect of irrigation pump sets.
? Supply of seeds to small and marginal farmers at 50% subsidy in drought affected 
regions.
? Minimum Support Price operations for Soya bean, Maize and Sunflower by the 
Agricultural Marketing Department in collaboration with NAFED.
? Educating farmers with the help of Psychologists and Social scientists about the ill 
effects of suicide and inculcate among them the confidence to stand up to any 
adversity.
? Encouragement to farmers to take up alternate crop in places where rainfall has failed 
and drought resistant varieties of crop can be grown.
? Implementation of Rashtriya Krishi Bima Yojana in the State from 2000-01 and 
admissible compensation till Kharif 2003 paid.
? Raitha Samparka Kendras to act as focal points to receive representations and 
complaints from farmers.
A sum of Rs. 204 lakhs have so far been sanctioned @ Rs. 1,00,000 for each 
family in respect of farmers who committed suicide during 2003-04. A sum of
 Rs. 36 lakhs has also been sanctioned and paid to the families of farmers who
 committed suicide during the current financial year i.e. 2004-05.
(c): The Prime Minister visited a few villages in Andhra Pradesh on
 1st July, 2004 and directed among other things, that livelihood cover should
 be provided to one person from each of the suicide affected families there 
through collaborative action between the Government and the banks. He also
announced an assistance of Rs. 50,000 from the PM`s National Relief Fund
 (PMNRF) to the families of persons who committed suicide.
(d) In order to mitigate the distressing situation of farmers due to
 the problem of indebtness, the Government of India on 18.6.2004 has announced
 a special package for providing credit related relief 
to the farmers. Following are the highlights of this announcement: -
? Total flow of agricultural credit which is estimated at Rs.80,000 crore
 in 2003-04 is to 
be enhanced to about Rs.1,05,000 crore in 2004-05 representing a 30 per cent
 increase over the flow of credit in the previous year.
? In order to provide credit to tenant farmers and oral lessees, NABARD to
 facilitate formation and financing of self-help groups of tenant farmers and
 oral lessees. This exploratory/pilot effort is expected to bring nearly a
 lakh of tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers within the banking
 fold.
? Scales of finance to be reviewed to meet the realistic credit needs of
 farmers, especially capital-intensive agricultural operations. 
? Debt restructuring to be done by commercial banks, RRBs and cooperatives 
in accordance with the new guidelines to be laid down by RBI/NABARD.
NABARD have issued directions to all State level cooperative institutions for
 fixation of realistic scales of finance to meet the credit requirements of the
 farmers for raising crops. Debt restructuring will be done by the 
commercial banks, RRBs and cooperatives in accordance with the new guidelines
 as in the following: -
Farmers in distress – Debts of farmers in districts declared as calamity-
affected by the State Government concerned will be rescheduled/restructured.
 Interest outstanding in the accounts of such borrowers will be clubbed with
 the principal outstanding on March 31, 2004, and the amount thus arrived at 
shall be repayable over a period of five years, at current interest rates,
 including an initial moratorium of two years.Farmers in arrears – Loans and
 advances outstanding as on 31st March, 2004 may be rescheduled into a term
 loan repayable over a period of three to five years at the current rates of
 interest. Interest outstanding as on 31st March, 2004 may be
 collected upfront. In case of term 
loans and previous rescheduled loan where the existing repayment schedule is
 longer than 3 to 5 years the overdue part of the principal shall only be
 rescheduled. The remaining part of the loan shall have originally contracted
 schedule of repayment. 
OTS for small and marginal farmers – Loans outstanding of the identified
 farmers whose accounts have been categorized, as NPAs as on 31.3.2001
 would be covered under the scheme. Eligible farmers should apply to
 bank in writing requesting for such settlement. For accounts declared 
as NPAs as on 31.3.2001, the settlement amount will be the balance outstanding 
in the loan account as on 31.3.2001. As regards interest accrued in the
 account after 31.3.2001, banks will decide upon the amount of compromise to be
 offered in each individual case subject to the condition that the
amount of compromise will not exceed the interest accrued in the account 
between 31st March, 2001 and date of settlement. 
The Reserve Bank of India has also issued standing guidelines to banks for
 providing relief to the farmers in areas affected by natural calamities.
 These guidelines envisage inter-alia:
? Conversion/ rescheduling of loans in the event of natural calamity for
 periods ranging from 3 to 9 years depending upon the successive crop failure/
 intensity of damage of crops. 
? Grant of fresh crop loans to affected farmers.
? Conversion of principal as well as interest due on the existing short
 term loans to medium term loans. 
? Grant of consumption loans. 
? Not to compound interest in respect of loans converted / rescheduled etc. 
? Not to charge penal interest in respect of current dues in default.

details:

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD)
(a) & (b): The fast growing telecom service sector in India has drawn attention of major international telecom companies for setting up of manufacturing facilities in India. As per the policy, no Government approval is required for setting up of manufacturing unit for the telecom sector.
(c) Some of the international telecom companies have given their recommendations for extending fiscal incentives and removal of certain impediments for the accelerated growth. However, the Government has already provided a number of incentives to promote investment in telecom manufacturing sector. Some of the incentive are:-
(i) 100% Foreign Direct Investment is allowed in this sector under automatic route through Reserve Bank of India (RBI). A technical know-how fee of

(ii) Electronic Hardware Technology Park Scheme had been modified to boost indigenous telecom manufacturing industry.

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(SHRI SRIPRAKASH JAISWAL)
(a) to (d): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 111 FOR 8.12.2004 REGARDING NAXALITES RISE AND MENACE IN KARNATAKA.
(a) & (b): The CPML-PW and its front bodies are spreading their activities on the issue of eviction of tribals from the Kudremukh National Park in Malenadu region, comprising the districts of Chikmagulur, Shimoga, Udupi, Dakshina Kannada, Hassan and Kodagu.
The Central Government has adopted a multi-pronged strategy to tackle the problem of naxalism which includes (a) having a peace dialogue by the affected States, wherever feasible, with naxal groups willing to abjure violence, (b) moderanisation and strengthening of the State Police forces, long term deployment of Para Military forces, intensified intelligence based well-coordinated anti-naxalite operations, (c) focused attention on integrated development of the affected areas and (d) removal of socio-cultural alienation of people, gearing up of public grievances redressal system and creation of Local Resistance Groups.
The Government of Karnataka is alive to the problem of naxlites spreading their activities to some parts of the State and has initiated suitable counter measures.
(c) & (d): The issue of dislocation and rehabilitation of the tribals has been taken up by the State Government which is also in touch with the Ministry of Forest and Environment and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

records.title: DECLINE IN WATER TABLE .
details:
(a) whether Government are aware of a recent report that
 declining water table may result in no ground water in major
 States like Delhi, in as few as 15 years;
(b) which are the top five worst performing States in terms of
decline of their water table; and
(c) what steps are being planned and taken by Government to
remedy the current situation?

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES 
(SHRI PRIYA RANJAN DASMUNSI)
(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF RAJYA
SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.96 FOR REPLY ON 07.12.2004 REGARDING
DECLINE IN WATER TABLE
(a) As per the studies carried out by Central Ground Water
Board (CGWB), under the Ministry of Water Resources, the fresh
water zones in some areas of Delhi will become unavailable for
exploitation within the next decade if the present rate of
exploitation of ground water continues. The worst affected areas
of Delhi are South West and South districts, which have been
notified by the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) for
control and regulation of ground water development. In South
West district where a lens of 10 to 30 meter potable water
floats over brackish water, the annual domestic draft is as high
as 134 MCM (Million Cubic Meter) and the ground water levels are
declining at the rate of 0.93 meter/year. In South district, the
maximum depth of water level has reached 59 meter and annual
decline of ground water level is about 0.7 meter with
domestic draft of about 82.6 MCM. 
(b) The top five worst affected States in terms of decline of
water table and over-exploitation of ground water resources are
Punjab, Delhi, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Haryana. 
(c) Water being a State subject, it is primarily the
responsibility of the concerned State Governments to take steps
to remedy the situation. Central Government has
initiated/planned following measures to check over-exploitation
and augmentation of ground water:-
(i) Circulation of a Model Bill in the year 1970 which was re-
circulated in 1992 and again in 1996 to all the States/Union
Territories to enable them to enact suitable legislation for
regulation and control of ground water development. 
(ii) Constitution of Central Ground Water Authority under the
Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 for regulation and control of
ground water management and development. The CGWA has notified
11 critical areas, including South and South West districts of
Delhi, on consideration of over-exploitation of ground water
resources. Further, the CGWA has also notified 32 over-exploited
areas in the country for registration of ground water
structures. 
(iii) In 673 over-exploited and 425 dark/critical areas in
the country, State Pollution Control Boards and Ministry of
Environment & Forests obtain No Objection Certificate (NOC) from
CGWA for any new industry/projects. A pre-condition for any
permission is the mandatory adoption of rain water harvesting
system by the industry/project for ground water recharge. 
(iv) On similar lines, other developmental projects located in
Coastal Regulation Zone obtain NOC from CGWA as pre-requisite
for environment clearance. 
(v) The CGWA has issued directions to Group Housing Societies,
Institutes, Hotels, Industries, Farm Houses etc., in the
notified areas of Delhi, Faridabad, Gurgaon and Ghaziabad to
adopt rain water harvesting system. 
(vi) Implementation of a Central Sector Scheme for Study of
Recharge to Ground Water in the country during the VIII & IX
Five Year Plans. 
(vii) The CGWB has proposed a Centrally Sponsored Scheme at
an estimated cost of Rs. 175 crores for Artificial Recharge to
Groundwater and Rainwater Harvesting during the remaining part
of the X Five Year Plan. 
(viii) Circulation of Manual/Guidelines on Artificial
Recharge of Ground Water to the States/Union Territories to
enable them to formulate area specific artificial recharge
schemes to check the declining trend of ground water levels. 
(ix) Central Ministries/Departments of Railways, Defence, Posts,
Telecommunications, Central Public Works Department and National
Highways Authority of India have been requested to provide roof
top rain water harvesting structures in the buildings under
their control. 
(x) States/UTs have been requested to provide water harvesting
structures in buildings under their administrative control. 
(xi) All the States/Union Territories have been requested for
advising the local bodies in their respective States/Union
Territories to allow rebate in property tax to persons, who
adopt roof top rainwater harvesting in their premises. 
(xii) The Ministry of Urban Development & Poverty
Alleviation has amended Building Bye-laws, 1983, making
provision for water harvesting through storing of water run-off
including rain water in all new buildings on plots of 100 square
meters and above in Delhi mandatory. 
(xiii) CGWB has provided technical guidance on rain water
harvesting to around 1800 agencies, including State Government
agencies, educational institutions, private entrepreneurs and
individuals. 
(xiv) Launching of a website on Roof Top Rain Water
Harvesting (www.cgwbindia.com) to make aware and educate the
public about various techniques of harvesting rainwater and
store it for future use. 
(xv) Organisation of mass awareness programmes and training
courses on rainwater harvesting and artificial recharge of
ground water. 
(xvi) Water conservation campaign has been launched keeping
in view the various target groups like youth and children,
women, farmers and villagers, policy and opinion makers.
Publicity through print media, telecasting of spots on the
television, broadcasting messages on radio, holding of seminars,
workshops, conferences etc., have been undertaken for the
purpose.

records.title: (clubbed) NATIONAL MANUFACTURING AND COMPETITIVENESS COUNCIL
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether it is a fact that Government have set up the 
 National Manufacturing and Competitiveness Council to advise 
 Government on measures to restructure Public Sector Enterprises 
 and on disinvestments;
(b) whether the Investment Commission and Board for 
 Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises proposed earlier 
 in the Budget 2004-05 are being set up;
(c) if so, whether it would not result in overlapping of 
 functions of these institutions; and
(d) whether any decision has been taken in this regard and 
 if so, the details thereof?

Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance ( Shri S.S. Palanimanickam)
(a) Yes, Sir. The Government has set up an autonomous National 
Manufacturing and Competitiveness Council under the administrative 
control of the Department of Industrial Policy & Promotion. However,
the mandate of this Council is not to advise the Government on 
measures to restructure Public Sector Enterprises and/or on
disinvestment, but to advise it on industrial and sector specific
initiatives required for enhancing competitiveness of Indian industry 
in areas like research and development, entrepreneurship promotion, 
infrastructure enhancing facilities, trade and fiscal policies and 
employment generation. 
(b) Yes, Sir. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved 
the setting up of an Investment Commission and the Board for 
Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises (BRPSE). 
( c ) & (d) The functions of the three institutions are not likely to 
overlap as each of them have distinct terms of reference. While the 
National Manufacturing and Competitiveness Council has been constituted 
to advise the Government on industrial and sector specific initiatives 
required for enhancing competitiveness of Indian industry, the BRPSE is
expected to advise the Government on ways and means for strengthening 
Public Sector Enterprises and to critically examine the proposals for 
revival, rehabilitation and reconstruction of sick or loss making Public
Sector Enterprises. On the other hand, the mandate of the Investment
Commission would be to make recommendations to the Government on both 
policy and procedures to facilitate greater foreign direct investment 
flows in India and to encourage investment in sectors where there is 
dire need for investment but adequate investment has not flowed so far.

THE MINISTER OF POWER
( SHRI P.M. SAYEED )
(a) : According to a press release of Associated Chambers of Commerce and 
Industries of India (ASSOCHAM), the power tariff subsidy granted to the agriculture sector 
has eroded the revenues of State Electricity Board to the extent of around Rs.20,000 crores in 
the last five years. Basis of this assessment is not available in this communication.
(b) : The Electricity Act, 2003 provides that the State Electricity Regulatory 
Commissions (SERCs) have the powers to fix tariff for sale of electricity to consumers taking 
into account the revenue requirement of distribution licensees. Section 65 of the Act provides 
that if the State Government requires the grant of any subsidy to any consumer or class of 
consumers in the tariff determined by the SERCs, the State Government shall pay to the 
concerned utility/licensees the full amount required to compensate the grant of subsidy. Thus, 
the matter of providing subsidy in tariff to a class of consumers is exclusively in the domain of 
the State Government.

(a) & (b): Prasar Bharati has informed that as on 16.08.2004 Doordarshan has

records.title: COMMITTEES ON RAILWAY ACCIDENTS .
details:
(a) whether the recommendations of various Committees including Prakash Narain Committee on Railway accidents have Since been considered and action taken on them; and
(b) if so, the details thereof ?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS
( SHRI R. VELU )
(a) & (b): A statement is attached.
STATEMENT REFERREDTO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1916 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 20-08-2004 REGARDING COMMITTEES ON RAILWAY ACCIDENTS.
(a) & (b): Between 1960 and 1980, three High Powered Committees viz. Railway Accidents Committee-1962 (Kunzru Committee), Railway Accidents Inquiry Committee - 1968 (Wanchoo Committee) and Railway :Accidents Enquiry Committee-1978 (Sikri Committee) went into the entire gamut of Railway working and suggested measures for improving the Railway Safety. Action for implementation of the accepted recommendations of these Committees was taken.
Thereafter, Railway Safety Review Committee i.e RSRC (Kharma Committee) had been set up in 1998 to, inter alia review the position of accidents on the Indian Railways and to review the implementation of the recommendations made by the earlier Committees and to make their own recommendations. The Railway Safety Review Committee made a total of 278 recommendations in both the parts of its report. Of the 242 recommendations, which have been accepted fully or partially, 92 have already been implemented. Other accepted recommendations are at various stages of implementation depending upon the availability of resources.
There was no Prakash Narain Committee on railway accidents. However, a National Transportation Safety Board had been set up in 1987 under the Cabinet Secretariat, with the main objective of bringing about improvements in safety in different transport sectors like Railways, Civil Aviation, Road Transport etc. This Board was wound up with effect from 1st April, 1990. Shri Prakash Narain was the Chairman of National Transportation Safety Board.
After-winding up the National Transportation Safety Board some recommendations pertaining to Railways were communicated to the Ministry of Railways on which action as warranted was taken.

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI E. AHAMED)

Government has been taking into account the need to benefit the Eastern and North-Eastern states in pursuing foreign policy goals with neighbouring countries in the East bilaterally as well as multilaterally through the regional grouping, Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) consisting of India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand.
The BIMSTEC Framework Agreement on Free Trade Area signed in October 2003 envisages FTA in goods, investment and services. For trade in services and investments, the negotiations shall commence in 2005 and are expected to be completed by 2007.

A framework FTA was signed with Thailand in October 2003 and an `Early Harvest Package` of 82 items will commence on September 1, 2004. details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

MINISTER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
( SHRI KAMAL NATH )
(a) Yes, Sir.
(b) Farm subsidies by United States was not specifically on the agenda of UNCTAD XI Conference. However, the need for elimination of all export subsidies by developed countries was emphasized by us in our discussions. The negotiated text adopted by the Conference emphasized, among other things, the need for reductions of, with a view to phasing out, all forms of export subsidies, and substantial reductions in trade-distorting domestic support.
(c) Yes, Sir.
(d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO 289 FOR 16th AUGUST 2004 REGARDING UNCTAD MEETING AT SAO PAULO
India along with other developing countries group known as G-77 and China, were successful in highlighting the concerns of developing countries under the multilateral trading system. India also participated in a G-20 meeting, along with countries such as Brazil, China, South Africa, Argentina etc., which was held in parallel to the UNCTAD deliberations. The main theme of the G-20 discussions was the need for preferential treatment for developing countries especially in the agricultural sector, in the on-going negotiations of the WTO. The developing countries succeeded in pointing out that the central issue of globalization should be development. It was also acknowledged that there is a need for policy space and policy flexibility for the development strategies of national Governments. It was decided that UNCTAD, which has provided an invaluable forum for advancing the inter-relationship between trade and development, from both the national and international perspective, across the three pillars of its mandate: independent policy analysis, technical assistance and consensus building, should continue its work and provide necessary inputs to the developing countries.

records.title: (clubbed) PROCESSING OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether Government are aware that only two per cent of
 the vegetables in the country are being processed at present
 as against 15-40 per cent in other countries;
(b) whether there is any proposal to reduce excise duty on
processed foods to boost the demand for the products in the
country;
(c) whether Government are contemplating to provide a
supporting network of infrastructure of roads, electricity,
transport and cold storage, etc. to the processed food
sector; and
(d) if so, the steps being contemplated to organize the
food processing industry on a modern and scientific basis to
ensure quality and cost efficiency in the industry?
 ANSWER

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI SUBODH KANT SAHAI)
(a) to (d): A statement is laid on the table of the
House.
Statement referred to in reply to Parts (a) to (d) of Rajya
Sabha Starred Question No. 178 for 16th July, 2004
regarding processing of fruits & vegetables.
(a) & (b): Level of processing of fruits & vegetables is
presently a little over 2% as against higher level of
processing in certain other countries. Processed products of
fruits & vegetables are already exempted from payment of
excise duty. For promotion of upcoming agro processing
units, the Government has announced on 8th July, 2004 in
Parliament to allow under Income Tax Act, a deduction of
100% of profit for five years and 25% of profits for the
next five years in case of new agro processing industries
set up to process, preserve and package fruits & vegetables.
Present excise duty of 16% on dairy machinery has been fully
waived. Excise duty on meat, poultry and fish products has
been reduced from 16% to 8%. Excise duty on food grade
hexane used in edible oil has been reduced from 32% to 16%.
(c) & (d): In order to ensure
better market orientation and make food processing units
more cost-competitive, financial assistance @ 25% for
general and 33.33% for difficult areas subject to maximum of
Rs. 4.00 crore is sanctioned for establishment of food parks
which provide common facilities such as uninterrupted power
supply, water supply, cold storage/ice plant, warehousing
facilities, affluent treatment plant, quality control and
analytical laboratories, training/conference facilities etc.
Financial assistance is also provided for establishment,
modernization and expansion of food processing units @ 25%
and 33.33% of costs of plant and machinery and technical
civil works subject to a maximum of Rs. 50 lakhs and Rs. 75
lakhs in general and difficult areas respectively. For
improvement of food quality/safety, financial assistance is
provided to units/organizations to enable them to adopt bar
coding practices, implement HACCP/ISO standards, set up
quality control lab, codex cell, etc. Keeping in view the
new approach and fresh thinking towards agro processing, the
Government has planed to act vigorously as a catalyst agent
to promote power arrangement and other networking facilities
in food parks.

records.title: ADDITIONAL AMBASSADOR LEVEL OFFICIAL AT INDIAN EMBASSY IN USA .
details:
(a) whether in addition to the Indian Ambassador in USA, another official of the same rank is operating in USA:
(b) if so, what specific role has been assigned to him particularly in regard to NRIs and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) in the USA: and
(c) the details of the action already taken and proposed to be taken by him in this regard?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI VINOD KHANNA)
a) There is only one official designated as the Ambassador of India to USA. However, two officers are designated in the rank of `Ambassador` for functional reasons, which includes Permanent Representative of India to UN, New York, and Special Adviser to the Permanent Mission of India and Ambassador-at-Large to NRIs/PIOs based in New York.
b) The Government of India appointed Ambassador-at-Large (AAL) for Non-Resident Indians(NRIs) and Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs), with the aim to strategically promote better coordination within the NRI/PIO community as well as economic cooperation, investment and commerce by NRIs/PIOs with India and other countries.
c) The mandate of Ambassador-at-Large for NRIs & PIOs is global and not limited to USA. Action taken and to be taken by his office, inter-alia include:-
(i) Visits to the countries with large diaspora presence to establish contact and network with various Indian organizations. 
(ii) Preparation of reports giving suggestions/proposals/ recommendations and organization of meetings and workshops covering youth and students, enhancement of India`s image in the ethnic media, inter-religious meet, Indo-Caribbean leadership forum and youth and diaspora students etc. A number of workshops in these areas are in the offing.
(iii) Functioning of a Grievances and Complaints Cell which attends to more than 1000 queries per month from all over the globe pertaining to diaspora issues, seeking information and Consular complaints.
(iv) Managing a website which provides NRI/PIO related information and about the services provided by AAL`s office.
(v) Organization of a Public Meeting for the Prime Minister with Indo-American community in September, 2003. More than 4000 participated in the meeting.
(vi) Promotion of Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD)-2003 and PBD-2004 for large scale diaspora participation.
(vii) Providing support and interaction base to visiting VIPs, Members of Parliament, State and Central Ministers with the NRI segment in socio-cultural, investment and other areas.

records.title: TASK FORCE ON INFRASTRUCTURE .
details:
(a) whether upgradation of major metro airports in India to
 world class standards was one of the mandates given by the
 Task Force on Infrastructure, set up by the Prime Minister
 in 1998; and
(b) if so, the details of progress made by the Ministry of
 Civil Aviation from 1998 till date in this respect?

MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION ( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY ) 
 (a):- Yes Sir.
 (b):- The Task Force on Infrastructure on 9.12.1998
 recommended that airports at Delhi, Mumbai and Bangalore be
 corporatised. Based on this recommendation, Government of
 India in January, 1999 decided to corporatise the airports
 at Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkota, besides construction
 of Greenfield Airports at Bangalore. Considering the
 complexitites involved in corporatisation, the Task Force on
 3.6.1999 approved the leasing route. Government of India in
 Janurary, 2000 approved restructuring of airports of
 Airports Authority of India through long term leasing route
 as and when found suitable. The airports at Delhi, Mumbai,
 Kolkota and Chennai were taken up for this exercise at the
 first instance. The Financial Consultant and Legal
 Consultant for restructuring exercise were appointed in
 March, 2000 and March, 2001 respectively. An
 Inter-Ministerial Group(IMG) was constituted to advise and
 monitor the entire exercise. The IMG met periodically to
 discuss and deliberate on various strategic issues.
 Pre-Investment Meets were held in New Delhi and London in
 April, 2002 to formally introduce the long term lease
 process. The Meet was attended by many Airport Operators,
 Financial Companies etc. An Amendment Bill was introduced in
 the Parliament on 30.11.2000 for incorporating and enabling
 provision in the Airports Authority of India (AAI) Act,
 1994 providing for leasing of airports. The Bill was
 referred to the Department Related Standing Committee on
 Transport, Tourism and Culture. The Committee tabled its
 report on 21.11.2002. As per the recommendations of the
 Committee, a comprehensive Airports Authority of India
 (Amendment) Bill, 2003 was introduced in the Parliament. The
 Bill was passed by Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha on 9.5.2003 and
 28.7.2003 respectively. Meanwhile, the restructuring through
 Joint Venture route was also considered. The Hon`ble Finance
 Minister, in Budget Speech 2003-04 has inter-alia announced
 that in addition to the existing initiatives for leasing of
 major airports, the Delhi and Mumbai airports will be taken
 up for modernisation to international standards through
 formation of two Joint Venture companies. Steps have been
 taken for incorporation of two separate companies for Delhi
 and Mumbai airports. The transaction structure is being
 finalised in consultation with Ministry of Finance.

records.title: PRIME MINISTER S VISITS
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that Prime Minister met Heads of Germany, China 
 and Russia during his visit abroad during May-June this year;
(b) If so, the details of the subject matters discussed and their response 
 thereto; and
(c) what has been their stand on the cross border terrorism by Pakistan and the Kashmir issue?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS
 (SHRI DIGVIJAY SINGH)
(a) Prime Minister had bilateral meetings with Mr. Gerhard Schroedar, 
German Chancellor on 28th May, 2003, in Berlin, Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation on 30 May, 2003 in St. Petersburg and with Mr. Hu Jintao, President of the People`s Republic of China on May 31, 2003 in St. Petersburg; 
(b) During his visit to Germany, PM held wide ranging discussions with the German leadership on bilateral relations and on regional and international issues of mutual interest. 
In his meeting with President Putin, Prime Minister discussed issues of bilateral, regional and international interest. The two leaders agreed that in accordance with the strategic partnership between the two countries, the extensive consultations between them should be continued. President Putin reiterated Russia`s commitment to further deepen defence relations with India. The two leaders agreed that there should a UN role in Iraq.
In the meeting with President Jintao, Prime Minister`s then forthcoming visit to China, global peace, stability, bilateral relations, situation in Iraq, role of the UN and PM`s initiative with respect to Pakistan were discussed. Both leaders agreed that China and India shouldered major responsibility for promoting world peace and stability, authority of the UN needed to be further strengthened and our Missions to UN should stay in touch regarding this and on Iraq. President Hu expressed confidence that PM`s visit to China would promote constructive and cooperative partnership. PM underlined the need for developing bilateral relations based on the Panchsheel and mutual sensitivity to each other`s concerns to resolve our differences.
(c) His interlocutors in Germany were sensitized to our concerns on the need for an immediate cessation of cross-border terrorism. There was unanimous appreciation for Prime Minister`s peace initiative. 
Russia has repeatedly stated that cross-border terrorism should be ended
and that the Kashmir issue should be settled bilaterally between India and
Pakistan in accordance with the Simla Agreement and the Lahore
Declaration.
Chinese President complimented and congratulated the Prime Minister of India on his peace initiative with respect to Pakistan. He said that the Chinese government supported any initiative to ease the situation and hoped that India and Pakistan would resolve their differences through dialogue and by peaceful means to make the situation in South Asia peaceful.

records.title: UNEMPLOYMENT PROBLEM
details:
MINISTER OF LABOUR
(SHRI SAHIB SINGH VERMA)
a) to d) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.268 BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA AND SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT REGARDING UNEMPLOYMENT PROBLEM FOR REPLY ON 7.8.2003.
Estimates of employment and unemployment are obtained through quinquennial labour force surveys conducted by National Sample Survey Organistion. Last such survey was conducted during 1999-2000. As per these surveys, estimated employment in the country on usual status basis has gone up from approximately 374 million in 1993-94 to 397 million in 1999-2000. Number of unemployed during 1993-94 and 1999-2000 was approximately 75 lakh and 90 lakh respectively.
 The Special Group headed by Dr. S.P.Gupta, Member, Planning Commission has recommended strategy and programmes which have been considered while formulating the 10th Plan, for targeting creation of 50 million employment opportunities (10 million per year) during the 10th Plan period (2002-2007). It identified the activities where there is a major potential of large new job opportunities as in agriculture, including social forestry, animal husbandry, fishing, horticulture and related areas and small and medium industries, construction, tourism, information technology, financial sector, education and health. The special Group has felt that with the target of achieving 10 million jobs per year, it will be possible to achieve near full employment situation by the end of 2012.
Organised Sector constitutes about 7% of the total employment in the country. Loss of jobs, if any ,in Public Sector Undertakings (PSU`s), disinvested PSU`s and industrial units, may not have any significant effect on total employment in the country.

(a) & (b) : Of the 150 exploratory wells drilled during 2002-03 by Oil & Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC), 46 wells are oil and gas bearing and 20 wells are gas bearing, whereas, of the 190 development wells drilled by them, 167 wells are oil and gas bearing and 7 wells are gas bearing.

records.title: (clubbed) LITERACY TARGET .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether UNESCO, which was initially optimistic about
India`s claims of total literacy by decade-end, has now started
expressing reservations;
(b) if so, whether a recent report of the UN body says
universal elementary education may elude the country even
around 2015, five years after the Government`s deadline;
(c) if so, what were the main reasons put forward by them; and
(d) what steps Government propose to take to see that India
achieves literacy target by 2015?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT 
(DR. SANJAY PASWAN)
(a) to (c) UNESCO has brought out a EFA Global Monitoring
Report, 2002 in which India has been shown at serious risk of
missing the EFA goals of Universal Primary Education and Total
Literacy by 2015. The conclusions drawn in this Report are
based on data available to UNESCO on the parameters of net
enrolment ratio in primary schools, gender parity as per gross
enrolment ratio in primary schools and the percentage of adult
literacy. The data used by UNESCO for these parameters were
either outdated or not available to UNESCO as far as India is
concerned. Further, initiatives taken in the recent years
like launch of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and
restructuring of literacy programmes have not been taken into
account for arriving at the conclusions.
(b) The initiatives of the Government for achieving the
literacy target include:-
1) The Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) to achieve
universalization of elementary education.
The objectives of SSA are:
- All children in school, Education Guarantee Centre,
Alternate School, `Back-to-School` camp by 2003
- All children complete five years of primary schooling by
2007
- All children complete eight years of elementary schooling
by 2010
- Focus on elementary education of satisfactory quality with
emphasis on education for life
- Bridge all gender and social category gaps at primary
stage by 2007 and at elementary education level by 2010
- Universal retention by 2010
2) The literacy schemes of the National Literacy Mission (NLM)
have been restructured to achieve continuity, efficiency
and convergence in the implementation of the Literacy
Campaigns and expansion in the scope of the Continuing
Education programme.
3) NLM aims to achieve a sustainable threshold level of 75%
literacy by 2007.

records.title: BANKS WITHOUT CMDS
details:
-
(a) the names of nationalised banks which are without CMDs at present;
(b) whether a number of new CMDs are likely to be appointed in the near future; and
(c) if so, the procedure/ Criteria/ guidelines laid down for appointing new CMDs?

FINANCE MINISTER (SHRI JASWANT SINGH) 
(a),(b) and (c):- A statement is placed on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO PARTS (a), (b) &(c) of RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION N0.25 FOR 22nd 
JULY. 2003 REGARDING BANKS WITHOUT CMDs BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA AND DR. ABRAR AHMED
a) Currently the posts of Chairmen and Managing Director in Allahabad Bank and Bank 
of India are lying vacant.
b) The anticipated vacancies of Chairmen and Managing Director of Nationalised Banks
upto 31.3.2004 are :-
I) CMD, Andhra Bank w.e.f. 1.11.2003
ii) CMD, Dena Bank w.e.f. 1.1.2004
iii) CMD, United Bank of India w.e.f. 1.3.2004 
(c) Appointment of CMDs in the Nationalised Banks are made in accordance with the 
provisions of Section 9(3) of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings)
Act 1970/1980. Government have, in addition, constituted an Appointments Board under the 
Chairmanship of Governor, Reserve Bank of India , Officials of Ministry of Finance and two
outside experts to consider eligible candidates and to make appropriate recommendations. 
These recommendations of the Appointments Board are then considered by the Government for 
final approval.
Appropriate criteria and procedure are laid down by the Appointments Board, from time to 
time. Copies of these criteria laid down in October, 2000, and in November, 2002 are 
enclosed at Annexures I and II respectively.
ANNEXURE-I
RELEVANT EXTRACTS FROM THE MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF THE APPOINTMENTS BOARD HELP IN RBL 
NEW DELHI ON 11th OCTOBER, 2000
Agenda Item No.2 Procedure for appointment of Whole time Directors in Public Sector Banks
The Appointments Board recognized the need for providing for a reasonable tenure for Whole 
Time Directors in public sector banks in order to ensure that the bank gets the benefit of 
continuity in leadership in an era of increasing competition along with a fair method of 
selection based on merit with due consideration to seniority, for maintaining the morale 
and motivation of employees. The issue of residual service for Chief Executive in an 
institution matters a lot, as a chief Executive with very short tenure implies lack of 
long-term commitment and vision and gaps in formulation and implementation of the long-term
policy for the organisation. It was also felt that the whole issue of Corporate Governance, 
which inter alia prescribes autonomy with accountability of the top management necessarily
demands a minimum reasonable tenure for Chief Executives, which will avoid uncertainty and 
ensure continuity of policy.
The Appointments Board also noted that the introduction of a procedure prescribing a minimum
tenure for appointment of whole time director will give rise to super-session of a few persons
with excellent record for the top position on ground of their residual service being less than 
the minimum prescribed. However, the situation of super-session of otherwise qualified and 
competent persons will emerge at any time, when a transition from merit-cum-seniority procedure
to tenure-oriented procedure is made. It was recognized that this may
create resentment among some persons and may impinge on building organisational teams at
higher levels.
The Appointments Board also recognized that the procedure for prescribing minimum tenure
for whole time directors in State Bank of India (SBI) keeping in view its special status, 
large size and trained and skilled manpower, may be somewhat different from the one which may 
be followed for the nationalised banks. Keeping in view the constraints of public sector 
character of these banks and the existing guidelines of Department of Personnel & Training,
the Appointments Board suggested that the following system may be followed by the Board while 
considering candidates for appointment as whole-time directors on the Boards of public sector
banks:-
a) For Chairman & Managing Director of SBI - a minimum residual service of two years from 
the date the vacancy arises.
b) For Managing Director of SBI - a minimum residual service of one year from the date the 
vacancy arises.
c) For Chairman and Managing Director of Nationalised Banks - All persons with minimum 
residual service of two years as on 1st April of the financial year in which vacancy arises 
will be considered. However, it should be kept in view that the person who is recommended for
a particular nationalised bank should as far as feasible, have at least two years of service
in the concerned bank.
d) For Executive Directors of Nationalised Banks - A minimum residual service of two years as
on Ist April of the concerned financial year shall be considered for the purpose of calling
people for interview.......`
Annexure-II
RELEVANT EXTRACTS FROM THE MINUTES OF THE MEETING OF THE APPOINTMENTS BOARD HELD IN RBI, 
NEW DELHI ON 25th NOVEMBER, 2002
`Agenda Item No.2 Appointment of CMDs of Nationalised Banks
The Board noted that the past practice has been to appoint CMDs from the existing Executive
Directors of nationalised banks based on seniority. The Board felt that the CMD being the 
head of the bank must be dynamic, possess leadership qualities and executive ability. The 
Board decided that a Committee comprising of Shri S. Narayan, Finance Secretary, Ms. Vineeta
Rai, Secretary (B&I), Dr. P. Kotaiah, Banking Expert and Prof. Abad Ahmed, Management Expert
may have interactions with the Executive Directors who have put in at least one year service 
as ED and with at least two years of service remaining as on 1st April, 2003 and recommend 
suitable names for appointment as CMDs for all the vacancies arising during the financial year 
1st April 2003 to 31st March, 2004. The Board further decided that the Government may separately
decide whether to confine selection of future vacancies to the existing Executive Director or
whether to widen the scope of selection by inviting applications from suitable professionals/
candidates through advertisement from the open market. Government may consider granting a 
compensation package to be offered to an open market candidate in order to attract best 
available talent. It was noted that the past experience of attracting outside candidates for 
top public sector positions at present salary levels was not every encouraging.

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRI A. RAJA) 
(a): A study was carried out at Delhi and Varanasi by Imperial College, London in partnership with 
(i) Shrshti; Delhi University; 
(ii) Banaras Hindu University, Varanasi; 
(ii) Development Tracks, New Delhi and 
(iv) Indian Agriculture Research Institute to assess the level of heavy metals in vegetables and to develop simple techniques, which could reduce heavy metal from these vegetables.
The studies revealed that vegetables crop are often grown in polluted and degraded environmental condition in the urban fringe zone and are subject to further pollution from vehicles and industries during marketing. 
The outcome of the studies in brief are as follows :-
`Fresh vegetables samples of cauliflower, okra, spinach were found to contain heavy metals higher than the permissible limits, as defined by PFA Act, 1954`.
A proportion of heavy metals in spinach samples were present on the surface of the leaves. After one washing 20 percent contamination is reduced and after second wash, it is reduced by approximately 50 percent.
(b) & (c): Regular intake of higher amount of metals in diet are injurious to health. There is a need to educate the farmers to adopt Good Agricultural Practices for production of crops including integrated pest management.

records.title: DECLINE IN TEXTILE EXPORTS .
details:
(a) what are the main reasons for continuous decline in India`s textile exports; and 
(b) the steps taken by Government to boost its export ?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF TEXTILES
SHRI BASANAGOUDA R. PATIL (YATNAL)
(a) The textile exports had recorded a growth of 10.1% in 1999-2000 and 14.6% in 2000-2001, but shown a negative growth of 11.0% in 2001-2002.
The major reason for negative growth of textile exports during the year 2001-02 were the reduced global demand triggered by the slowdown in the economies of some of our major trading partners like US, increasing polarization of world trade, formation of preferential trading blocks and stiff competition from low cost suppliers like Bangladesh, China, etc. 
As per the available DGCIS export data, the textile exports during the period April-December 2002 have amounted to US$ 8849.4 million which when compared with the exports of US$ 7814.6 million during the corresponding period of 2001 show a growth of 13.2%. This indicates the downtrend in textile exports has been reversed and they are back on path of export growth. 
(b) Government have been taking a number of measures to boost textile exports. Some of the important initiatives are:-
(i) The Government has de-reserved the woven segment of readymade garment from the SSI sector. It has also raised the SSI investment limit for knitted segment to Rs. 5 crores. 
(ii) The Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS) has been made operational from 1-4-1999 to facilitate the modernisation and upgradation of the sector. 
(iii) Weaving, processing and garment machinery, which are covered under TUFS, have been extended the facility of accelerated depreciation at the rate of 50%. Cost of machinery has also been reduced through Fiscal Policy measures. This further encourages modernisation. 
(iv) With a view to encouraging backward integration, the custom duty on shuttleless looms and other important textile machinery items has been brought down to 5%. 
(v) National Institute for Fashion Technology (NIFT), its six branches and Apparel Training & Design Centres (ATDCs) are running various courses/programmes to meet skilled manpower requirements of textile industry especially apparel in the field of design, merchandising and marketing. 
(vi) Facilities by way of eco-testing laboratories have been created to enable exporters to get the garments/textiles pre-tested for conforming to the requirements of importing countries. 
(vii) The Government has launched a centrally sponsored scheme titled `Apparel Park for Export Scheme` for imparting focused thrust for setting up of apparel manufacturing units of international standards at potential growth centres and to give fillip to exports. 
(viii) For upgrading infrastructure facilities at important textile centers, a scheme `Textile Centre Infrastructure Development Scheme (TCIDS) has been launched.

records.title: COOPERATIVE BANKS WITHOUT LICENCE
details:
(a) the number of Co-operative Banks operating in the country without requisite licence 
from Reserve Bank of India as on date;
(b) whether the matter of such unauthorized banks has been taken with concerned State 
Governments; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

(Minister of Finance & Company Affairs) (Shri Jaswant Singh)
`(a), (b) & (c):
A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.
Statement laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha in reply to parts (a), (b) & (c) of Starred 
Question No. 557 for 29th April. 2003 tabled by Shri Rajeev Shukla and Dr. Abrar Ahmed 
regarding Co-operative Banks without licennce. 
(a), (b) & (c): As reported by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and National Bank for Agriculture 
& Rural Development (NABARD), at present there are 17 State Cooperative Banks (SCBs), 296 
District Central Co-operative Banks (DCCBs) and 112 Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs) are 
operating in the country without licence from Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Since Co-operative 
Banks were brought under the ambit of Banking Regulation Act 1949 from 1st March, 1966, these 
Banks are permitted to carry on banking business till a decision is taken on their licence 
applications by RBI. In respect of the Banks which are likely to comply with the licence norms 
in the near future/ RBI has considered it advisable to give time to do the needful. Apart 
from these, there are 58 co-operative societies (54 in Kerala, 1 in Assam and 3 in Manipur) 
carrying on banking business without licence from RBI, on the basis of registration given by 
Registrar of Co-operative Societies(RCS) of the respective states. In addition, there are 
entities, one in Orissaand the other one in Uttar Pradesh, carrying on banking business 
unauthorisedly.
RBI has taken up the cases of unlicensed Banks with the respective State Governments. Some 
unlicensed Urban Co-operative Banks in Kerala have filed writ petition in the High Court of 
Kerala to quash the circular issued by the Registrar of Cooperative Societies of Kerala on 23rd 
January, 2003 to all joint Registrar of Co-operative Societies in the Districts and registered 
unlicensed Co-operative Urban Banks to stop any violation of Banking Regulation Act and to 
change their constitution to Urban Cooperative Societies by making necessary changes in their 
by-laws within two months. The Court issued an interim direction on 24th March, 2003 restraining
the State of Kerala from taking any coercive steps for non-compliance of the circular dated 
23rd January, 2003.

records.title: SINO INDO RELATIONS .
details:
(a) whether Sino-Indo relations were discussed
 at 5th Asian Security Conference at Delhi,
 late January;
(b) whether Defence Minister who spoke at the
 meet described China as having great potential
 for mutually beneficial economic relations
 with India;
(c) whether the meet saw hope of improving
 political relations with China despite the
 border dispute;
(d) what is the status of the border dispute
 and how Government hopes to settle it; and
(e) does the Government hope to push economic
 relations, putting the border dispute in the
 backburner?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE (PROF. CHAMAN
LAL GUPTA)
MINISTRY OF DEFENCE
(a) to (e): The 5th Asian Security Conference
on “Asian Security and China in the period
2000-2010” was organised by the Institute for
Defence Studies and Analyses in New Delhi from
27th to 29th January, 2003. India-China
relation was not per se included in the theme
of discussions at the Conference. However,
while delivering the concluding address there,
Raksha Mantri had expressed optimism that
India and China would arrive at consensus
through continuous dialogue and accommodation
of competing interests in the near future. He
had also observed that China had made good
progress on economic front in the last two
decades and India might learn a lesson
from them on this front.
Although contentious issues like the
boundary problem between the two countries are
to be settled, the economic relation between
them has been showing an upswing.
As regards boundary dispute between India
and China, the two sides have been discussing
the boundary question based on the
institutional framework provided by the two
Agreements signed by them in 1993 and 1996
with the objective of seeking a mutually
acceptable settlement of the issue.

records.title: NATIONALISATION OF WATER RESOURCES .
details:
(a) whether Tamil Nadu Government has protested against the
Kerala Government’s reported proposal to build dams across some
rivers flowing between the two States;
(b) whether the Central Government propose to consider a long-
standing demand of nationalising the water resources in view of
such disputes which have increased in the recent past; and
(c) if not, what other measures Government are contemplating to
improve the situation?

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI ARJUN CHARAN SETHI) 
(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (c) OF THE STARRED
QUESTION NO. 456 TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.4.2003 IN RAJYA SABHA
REGARDING NATIONALISATION OF WATER RESOURCES
(a): In December, 2002, the State of Tamil Nadu has written to
the Central Government regarding launching of a new scheme of
constructing a weir across river Bhavani near Mukkali village to
divert water to the west outside the Cauvery basin by the State
of Kerala and requested Central Government to take up the matter
with Government of Kerala and prevail upon it for not proceeding
in any manner with the construction of the proposed weir.
Subsequently, the State of Tamil Nadu has filed Petitions before
the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal(CWDT) objecting to the
undertaking of the construction of the scheme by the State of
Kerala. The CWDT has on April 2, 2003 directed the State of
Kerala that during the pendency of the proceeding before the
CWDT, the State of Kerala shall not proceed further with the
construction of the weir leading to trans basin diversion and
shall maintain the status quo as it was existing on 7.2.2003.
(b) & (c): The mechanism for resolution of the Inter-State Water
disputes exist in the form of Inter-State Water Disputes(ISWD)
Act, 1956, enacted under Article 262 of the Constitution. The
ISWD Act, 1956 has been amended on March 28, 2002 to provide for
time-bound adjudication of the dispute by the Tribunals. Also as
per the amended Act, the decision of the Tribunal after its
publication in the Official Gazette shall have the same force as
an Order or decree of the Supreme Court.

records.title: RATE OF ENTERTAINMENT TAX FOR CINEMA HALLS .
details:
(a) whether there has been a uniform rate of entertainment tax for cinema halls 
throughout the country; and
(b) if not, the efforts Government have made in this regard and the results 
thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION AND 
BROADCASTING (SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)
(a) Entertainment Tax is a State subject and the rates vary from State to State.
(b) With the objective of all round development of film industry, State 
Governments were inter-alia requested to consider rationalising the rates of 
Entertainment Tax so that a uniform rate prevails in the country. However, no 
consensus was arrived at in the matter and during the 24th Conference of State and 
Union Territory Information Ministers held in New Delhi on 21.1.2001, it was 
decided to set up a Committee for Development of the Entertainment sector, to 
suggest the policy framework both at the Centre and in the States for realising the 
potential of the Entertainment Sector. As a result of the deliberations in this 
Committee, it has been decided to recommend that all State/Union Territory 
administrations fix a ceiling of 60% on entertainment tax. The recommendations of 
the Committee have been circulated to all States/Union Territory Administrations.
______

records.title: VIDEO PIRACY IN FILM INDUSTRY .
details:
(a) the measures Government have taken to save the film industry from video piracy; and
(b) the results achieved so far?

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION & BROADCASTING 
(SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)
(a) & (b) The Copyright Act, 1957, which falls under the purview of the Ministry of Human 
Resource Development provides the legal basis for the subsistence of copyright in 
cinematograph films and music. The responsibility for dealing with offences under the 
Copyright Act rests with the police authorities of the State Governments and Union Territory 
Administrations. Copyright Enforcement cells have been set up in most States/UT 
Administrations headed by a senior police officer to deal with such offences.
The Copyright Act is amended from time to time to keep it in consonance with International 
Copyright Law.
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has taken several initiatives to mitigate piracy of 
films as follows:
(i) On the basis of a recommendation made by the Committee for 
Development of the Entertainment Sector, the Indian Institute of Mass 
Communication has been asked to formulate appropriate training 
modules for police officers to train them for anti-piracy work.; 
(ii) To create an anti-piracy mind-set and to promote cooperation among 
stakeholders, this Ministry had brought film producers, multi-service 
operators and cable operators together, and they had jointly resolved not 
to exhibit films without valid permission from the copyright holders. 
(iii) In an effort to check cable piracy, the Cable Television Networks 
Regulation Act has been amended in 2000, enabling the Government to 
prohibit a Cable operator from transmitting or re-transmitting any 
programme or channel for which he has not been granted a license by 
the Copyright holder. 
(iv) A recommendation made by the Committee for Development of the 
Entertainment Sector, that a realistic ceiling level for entertainment tax to 
be imposed by the State Governments could be 60%, since high rate of 
entertainment tax facilitates piracy, has been communicated to all State 
Governments.

records.title: RETURN AND REHABILITATION OF KASHMIRI MIGRANTS
details:
(a) whether any action plan for the return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants have been prepared; and
(b) if so, the status of the plan?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI HARIN PATHAK)
(a ) & (b): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
 STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (A) AND (B) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION No. 302 ( POSITION NO.2) FOR REPLY ON MARCH 12, 2003.
(a) & (b): In order to enable safe and honourable return of migrants to their native places in the Valley, the then State Government of J&K had finalized an Action Plan involving a total amount of Rs. 2589.73 crores. The Union Government has agreed to reimburse costs borne by the State Government as per approved norms in the case of those Kashmiri migrants who actually return to the Valley. The Action Plan is to be implemented in phases which envisages return and rehabilitation of migrant families in areas where clusters of migrant houses are available and in villages/mohallas in the Kashmir Valley Districts with sizeable Kashmiri Pandit population and where security is already being provided. To begin with, 166 houses forming 15 clusters were identified in Srinagar and Badgam Districts, which are considered safe for the return of the owners of these houses. The list of these clusters was published in the newspapers and steps were taken to identify the families and find their willingness to return to their homes. About 50 families who were registered with the Relief organization, Jammu were contacted personally to give their consent for return to the Valley on the basis of the package announced by the Government. Interaction meetings with some of these families were also held but as reported by State Government, only two families (not belonging to the particular area) have agreed to return to the Valley so far.
 The new State Government has indicated that it has identified the shrines in Mattan and Kheer Bhavani where the Kashmiri migrants displaced from these places could be settled temporarily by developing two model clusters containing temporary shelters for Kashmiri migrants, till such time they can repair their existing residential houses. Ministry of Finance has agreed to provide a grant of Rs. 10 crores to the State Government for the reconstruction/renovation of houses and shrines at Kheer Bhavani and Mattan.

records.title: CRITERIA FOR WORLD HERITAGE SITES .
details:
(a)
what is the criteria laid down for considering sites as World Heritage Sites; and 
(b)
the sites selected for the purpose for the year and progress made thereon?

MINISTER FOR TOURISM AND CULTURE (SHRI JAGMOHAN)
(a)
The criteria are enclosed as per Annexure.
(b)
Rock-cut shelters at Bhimbetka, District Raisen, Madhya Pradesh has been nominated for inclusion in the UNESCO World Heritage List for the year 2003. 
The Bhimbetka Site has been evaluated in November 2002 by ICOMOS, an agency engaged by UNESCO.
 ANNEXURE
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART PART (a) TO THE RAJYA SBAHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.749 TO BE ANSWERED ON 25.2.2003
 A monument, group of buildings or site which is nominated for inclusion in the World Heritage List will be considered to be of outstanding universal value for the purpose of the Convention when the Committee finds that it meets one or more of the following criteria and the test of authenticity. Each property nominated should therefore;
(a) 
(i) represent a masterpiece of human creative genius; or 
(ii) exhibit an important interchange of human values, over a span of time or within a cultural area of the world, on developments in architecture or technology, monumental arts, town-planning or landscape design; or 
(iii) bear a unique or at least exceptional testimony to a cultural tradition or to a civilization which is living or which has disappeared; or 
(iv) be an outstanding example of a type of building or architectural or technological ensemble or landscape which illustrates (a) significant stage(s) in human history; or 
(v) be an outstanding example of a traditional human settlement or land-use which is representative of a culture (or cultures), especially when it has become vulnerable under the impact of irreversible change; or 
(vi) be directly or tangibly associated with events or living traditions, with ideas, or with beliefs, with artistic and literary works of outstanding universal significance (the Committee considers that this criterion should justify inclusion in the List only in exceptional circumstances and in conjunction with other criteria cultural or natural);
and 
(b) 
(i) meet the test of authenticity in design, material, workmanship or setting and in the case of cultural landscapes their distinctive character and components (the committee stressed that reconstruction is only acceptable if it is carried out on the basis of complete and detailed documentation on the original and to no extent on conjecture). 
(ii) have adequate legal and/or contractual and /or traditional protection and management mechanisms to ensure the conservation of the nominated cultural properties or cultural landscapes. The existence of protective legislation at the national, provincial or municipal level and/or a well-established contractual or traditional protection as well as of adequate management and/or planning control mechanism is therefore essential and, as is clearly indicated in the following paragraph, must be stated clearly on the nomination form. Assurances of the effective implementation of these laws and/or contractual and/or traditional protection as well as of these management mechanisms are also expected. Furthermore, in order to preserve the integrity of cultural sites, particularly those open to large numbers of visitors, the State Party concerned should be able to provide evidence of suitable administrative arrangements to cover the management of the property, its conservation an!
d its accessibility to the public.

records.title: AVAILABILITY OF BANNED MEDICINES .
details:
(a) whether Government are aware that many drugs that are banned in 
several countries are freely available in India;
(b) if so, whether Government have made inquiries in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS (SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH DHINDSA )
(a) to (c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (a) to (c) OF RAJYA SABHA 
STARRED QUESTION NO.78 FOR ANSWER ON 21.2.2003.
(a), (b) and (c): Drugs withdrawn in some countries can continue to be 
used by other countries. The decision rests on various factors such as the 
disease pattern in a country, the varying reactions of certain ethnic groups in 
a given population to the drug and the availability of safer substitutes as well 
as the cost factor involved in the treatment of a particular disease. There is 
no system of global banning of drugs. There is an adequate mechanism to 
review the status of drugs in India as and when any serious adverse event is 
reported in international journals or WHO newsletters etc. 75 categories of 
drugs/drug formulations have so far been prohibited in the country.
The drug or formulations discontinued in developed countries are 
assessed by an expert committee in consultation with leading experts in 
given specializations. Based on their advice, the matter is placed before the 
Drug Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), a statutory body which comprises 
representatives from the medical profession, the State Drug Enforcement 
Authorities, experts, institutions, agencies that advise the government on 
technical issues related to the implementation of Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 
1940 and rules there under.

details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(c) whether Government have recently started Water Management plans for villages involving Panchayats; and
(d) if so, the details thereof ?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR RURAL DEVELOPMENT (SHRI ANNASAHEB M.K.PATIL)
i 
(a) & (b) : Yes Sir, Hon`ble Prime Minister has launched a new initiative namely `Hariyali` on 27.1.2003. Under this initiative, all watershed development programmes (DPAP, DDP and IWDP) of the Department of Land Resources would be implemented through Panchyati Raj Institutions (PRI). The basic features of `Hariyali` are given below:
Under this initiatve, the Gram Saabha would replace the Watershed Association and the Gram Panchyat would be execute the watershed project with technical support from the Block Panchayat who would act as the Project Implementing Agency (PAI) for all watershed projects in a particular Block. In case the Block/Zilla Panchyat has no technical staff to support the Gram Panchyats, suitable Government Line Department/Autonomous Agency may be identified for the purpose. Failing all these options, a reputed voluntary organization (NGO) of good operational/financial standing in the district with adequate technical expertise and experience may be identified to act as the PIA.
At the present rates of allocation to the existing watershed programmes of the Department, an amount of Rs. 1000 crore would be available annually to support execution of watershed projects through the PRIs. Detailed Guidelines for operationalizing this new initiative are under preparation. The provision of this initiative applicable to all the new watershed development projects that would be sanctioned in future. The on-going watershed projects will continue to be implemented under the prevailing Guidelines.

STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (d) OF

In response to the matter raised by the

details:

(b) if so, the details thereof?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)
(a) Yes, Sir.
(b) The committee has recommended detailed guidelines about strategies needed to be adopted
by the State Licensing Authorities for focused monitoring activities to curb the menace of 
manufacture and sale of spurious drugs. These strategies included establishment of intelligence
-cum-legal cell and anti spurious squad to detect and unearth spurious drugs cases; to set 
up/reactivate state drugs advisory committee in which all stake holders are partners; speedy 
analysis of drugs samples by the testing labs; undertaking surveillance of suspected dealers 
through decoy customers/ watchers; training programmes for officers of drugs control 
administration in matters concerning development of intelligence; detection, investigation; 
preparing and filing complaints, courts procedures; efficient communication networking through 
computerization; making stricter provisions under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 for offences 
non-bailable and non-cognizable; speedy trial by identified or designated courts for deciding
spurious drug case etc.

records.title: (clubbed) CHILD LABOURERS .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LABOUR 
(SHRI ASHOK PRADHAN)
(a): Authentic information on child labour in the country is generated by the decennial 
census. According to the 1991 census, the number of working children in India was 11.28 million.
The figures of the 2001 census have not yet been published.
(b): Government of India has taken steps for withdrawal and rehabilitation of child labour 
working in hazardous occupations to reduce the incidence of child labour in a particular 
district through the Scheme of National Child Labour Projects (NCLPs). Under the Scheme of 
NCLP, special schools have been set up in the child labour endemic districts with the provision 
for non-formal/formal education, vocational training, stipend, nutrition, health-care etc. So 
far, 100 NCLPs have been sanctioned in 13 child labour endemic districts for coverage of 2.11 
lakh children. As per the information available, 1.45 lakh children (approx.) have already been 
mainstreamed into the formal school system.
(c) & (d): The Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986 prohibits employment of
children in occupations and processes listed in the schedule to the Act and regulates it in all
other employments.
 The issue regarding amendment of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986
has been discussed in several fora including the Conference of the State Labour Ministers. 
Important suggestions made in the conference to make the Act more stringent include (a) making 
the offence a cognizable one; (b) making the penalties more stringent and deterrent; and (c)
the responsibility as to the proof of age of a child being made that of the employer. Amendment
of the Act is an ongoing process. As of now, no definite time frame can be indicated for 
amendment of the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986.

records.title: (clubbed) REHABILITATION PLANS FOR KASHMIRI MIGRANTS
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether any action plan for the return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants have been prepared by the Centre in consultation with State Government of Jammu and Kashmir; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
( SHRI CH.VIDYASAGAR RAO)
(a) & (b): In October 2000, Government of Jammu and Kashmir submitted an Action Plan for the Return and Rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants involving a total amount of Rs. 2589.73 crores to enable 52, 689 families of Kashmiri migrants comprising about 1.25 lakhs souls at present residing in Jammu, Delhi and other States/UTs to return to the Valley. The Action Plan envisages rehabilitation grant per family @ Rs. 1.50 lakhs; grant for repair of houses @ Rs. 1 lakh for houses intact and Rs. 3 lakhs for houses damaged; grant for household goods @ Rs. 0.50 lakhs and furniture @ Rs. 0.50 lakhs; interest free loan @ Rs. 1-2 lakhs per person; compensation for loss of income from agriculture upto Rs. 1.50 lakhs per family; interest free loan of Rs. 1.50 lakhs per family for investment in agricultural operations and sustenance of Rs. 2,000/- per month for one year.
 The Action Plan is proposed to be implemented by State Government in phases, which envisages return and rehabilitation of migrant families in areas where clusters of migrant houses are available and in villages/mohallas in the Kashmir Valley Districts with sizeable Kashmiri Pandit population and where security is already provided. To begin with, 166 houses forming 15 clusters had been identified by the State Government in Srinagar and Badgam Districts, which are considered safe for the return of the owners of these houses. The list of these clusters was published in the newspapers and steps were taken to identify the families and find their willingness to return to their homes. About 50 families who were registered with the Relief organization, Jammu were contacted personally to give their consent for return to the Valley on the basis of the package announced by the Government. Interaction meetings with some of these families were also held but none of the families have agreed to return to the Valley so far.
``
