records.title: (clubbed) CONTROL ON POPULATION .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE 
(SHRI SHATRUGHAN SINHA)
(a)to(d): A statement is laid on the table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 184 FOR 2.12.2002
.....
The measures adopted to control population by the Government have yielded favourable 
results. The Total Fertility Rate has come down from 6 in 1951 to 3.2 in 1999. The Birth 
Rate has come down from 40.8 in 1951 to 25.8 during the year 2000, as per the estimates of 
Sample Registration System(SRS), Registrar General of India. According to National Family 
Health Survey conducted in 1998-99, about 42% of the couples with two children and about 
58% of couples with 3 children have adopted terminal methods of contraception. The child 
population (0-6 years) has come down from 18% in 1991 to 15% in 2001 census, showing 
decline in fertility rate.
Among the major States with more than 20 million population, the States of Kerala and 
Tamil Nadu have already achieved a replacement level of fertility of a TFR of 2.1, while 
the States of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Orissa, Punjab and West 
Bengal are having a TFR of 2.2 to 3.0 and are in the direction of replacement level of 
fertility. There are 4 States viz. Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Chattisgarh and Haryana which 
are having a TFR of 3.1 to 4.0, while the 4 States of Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and 
Jharkhand have recorded a TFR of 4.1 to 4.7 as per the SRS, 1999.
Regarding the acceptance of terminal methods, the percentage of couples with two children 
have high acceptance in southern and western regions, being 60% in Tamilnadu, 72% in Andhra 
Pradesh, 50% in Maharashtra and 60% in Karnataka, while in Northern States, the acceptance 
is on the lower side in the States of U.P. (11%) & Bihar (18%). Similarly the percentage of 
couples with 3 children accepting terminal methods ranges between 65% to 85% in southern and 
western States, while in northern States of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, the range is between 24 to
31% as per NFHS 1998-99.
The proportion of Child population aged 0 to 6 years also follows a similar pattern. 
Tamilnadu has the lowest child population of 11% and Bihar with the highest of 20% as 
per census 2001.
As regards introduction of new methods of family planning in the current financial year, 
the Government has introduced an advanced version of Intra Uterine Device Cu.T 380 A, 
which remains effective for ten years. Emergency Contraceptive Pills, which is hormonal 
contraceptive that can be used to prevent pregnancy following an unprotected act of sexual 
intercourse within the past 72 hours, is also included in the programme.
In addition, research work is being carried out for injectible contraceptive CYCLOFEM, 
injection on male contraceptive (RISUG) and praneem as microbicidal and contraceptive.
.....

records.title: (clubbed) CLEANLINESS IN RAILWAY COACHES .
details: Clubbed question in this member’s official feed

(a) whether it is a fact that cleanliness , maintenance and upkeep of rail coaches are 
not upto the mark, causing inconvenience to the rail passengers; and
(b) if so , the steps taken by Government to improve the situation ?

MINISTER OF RAILWAYS (SHRI NITISH KUMAR) 
(a) & (b) : A statement is laid on the Table of the Sabha.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) & (b) OF STARRED QUESTION NO. 166, BY DR. ABRAR 
AHMED AND SHRI EAJEEV SHUKLA TO BE ANSWERED IN RAJYA SABHA ON 29.11.2002 REGARDING CLEANLINESS 
IN RAILWAY COACHES. 
(a) & (b): All railway passenger coaches are properly maintained, cleaned and attended prior 
to commencement of journey from the base station . Trains are also cleaned at nominated 
enroute ` ,. stations while traveling safaiwalas are provided on-selected trains for cleaning 
on the run. However, owing to intensive use and long continuous journeys, coaches become dirty 
on run despite enroute cleaning arrangements. Also, careless use, vandalism and lack of civic 
sense prevailing in certain
 `
regions and some-trains negate the Railway`s efforts in keeping the coaches clean and tidy
In order to meet the increasing passenger aspirations and to bring about further improvements, 
several new initiatives have been taken in the recent times as enumerated below:
i) Strengthening enroute cleaning arrangements by providing mechanized cleaning facilities 
under `Clean Train Station` scheme at identified 15 stations on major trunk routes. 
ii) Introduction of environment friendly, controlled discharge toilets in order to avoid 
station area being polluted by toilet discharge.
iii) Development of automatic exterior washing facility for trains at busy terminals. 
iv) Pest control on all coaches once a month through specialized agencies. 
v) Introduction of biodegradable waste disposal bags as a part of Clean Train Station 
scheme. vi) Introduction of `State of the Art` modular toilets in place of conventional 
toilet for all classes of coaches. These toilets are user friendly, elegant, easy to clean 
and pilferage proof. 
vii) Provision of 110 Volts electrical fittings in place of conventional 24 Volts 
and use of
fluorescent fittings in place of bulbs. viii) Introduction of Jan Shatabdi type services 
in which second class coaches have upper class
like feature including ergonomic chairs, noise control, modular toilets, rail mart, improved
flooring etc. 
ix) Indigenous manufacture of modem technology LHB type coaches with advance 
feature including screw less fibre reinforced plastic interiors, modular toilets 
with control discharge system which does not dirty the station area, electronic taps and 
toilet fittings, environment
control air-conditioning, ergonomic seats, superior ride comfort, noise insulation etc. 
x) Provsion of adequate maintenance time and manpower at base depot for maintenance and
cleaning for all new trains and progressive rationalization for all existing trains

records.title: FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE TO MERITORIOUS SPORTS PERSONS .
details:
(a) whether Government are aware of the sad state of affairs of many retired sports persons 
who had represented India at the national/international levels;
(b) if so, whether Government have floated any scheme to help them; if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have made any provision for development of meritorious players at the 
national and international levels; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the criteria being followed for providing financial 
assistance to such players?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI PON. RADHAKIRISHNAN) 
(a) Yes, Sir. From time to time proposals are received from the outstanding sportsperson of 
yesteryears living in indigent conditions for financial assistance 
(b) Yes, Sir. Under the following schemes, Government provides financial assistance to the 
outstanding/meritorious Sportspersons:- 
(i) National Welfare Fund For Sportspersons: Under the scheme. Government gives monthly 
pensions upto Rs. 2500/- and one time lump-sum financial assistance upto Rs. 40,000/- for 
medical treatment to the retired sportspersor who have represented the country at national/
international levels and living in indigent circumstances, i.e. whose monthly income is less 
than Rs. 3,000/-from all sources. 
(n) Sports Fund for Meritorious Sports Persons: Under the scheme, meritorio Sportspersons 
who have won medals in Olympic Games and Gold medal
World Cups/World Championships in Olympic and Asian Games disciplines are sanctioned monthly 
pensions @ Rs. 2500/- . Silver and Bronze medallists of World Cups/World Championships in 
Olympic and Asian Games disciplines and Commonwealth Games are sanctioned pension @ Rs, 2000/-
per month. Pension is sanctioned from the age of 30 years for lifetime. 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) In order to prepare the sportspersons to compete at National & International level, 
Government provides Financial Assistance to the various National Sports Federations and 
Sportspersons under the following schemes: 
(i) Assistance to National Sports Federations:- Under this scheme National Sports 
Federations are provided financial assistance for organization of National Coaching Camps, 
participation of athletes in International tournaments and engagement of foreign coaches and 
experts for meritorious sportspersons of National and International levels. 
(ii) Assistance to Promising Sports Persons and Supporting Personnel:- Under this scheme 
financial assistance upto Rs. 5 lakhs is sanctioned to a promising sports person, who has 
equaled or excelled the existing national record or is a gold medallist of last National 
Championship or is a medallist of Asian/Commonwealth Games/Afro-Asian Games/Olympic Games/
World Championship in different sports disciplines for undergoing training abroad, purchase 
of sports equipment, obtaining scientific support, and for training and participation in 
tournaments in the country. To get the assistance under the scheme, promising sportspersons 
should not be more than 25 years of age. For sports like shooting, golf, billiards and snooker, 
chess and yachting the age limit may be relaxed upto 35 years. 
(iii) National Sports Development Fund:- Meritorious Sportspersons seeking assistance under 
the scheme are also provided Financial Assistance for training.

(b) (c) and (d): During 1975 it was Family Planning Programme focussing only on population control. There has been a paradigm shift in the Family Welfare Programme after the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD), Cairo in 1994. The `Target Free Approach (TFA) was adopted since 1st April, 1996 all over India. This approach leaves the choice of family size to the couples themselves. Consequently the emphasis of programme has now shifted to publicity on first child birlth at proper age, adequate spacing among the issues, Immunisation and availability of both permanent and temporary methods of family planning. fixed for the laxity; and
(d) the number of known HIV cases in Manipur at present and
the action being taken to stop spreading of the dreaded
disease?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF

Manipur during the last three years is as below:-
1999 61
2000 364
2001 307
(b) No, Sir. 
(c) Question does not arise. 
(d) The cumulative number of HIV/AIDS cases in Manipur as
on 31-03-2002 is 1095. Government has launched a
comprehensive AIDS prevention and control programme which is
a 100% centrally sponsored scheme being implemented in all
States/UTs including Manipur through States/UTs. AIDS
Control Societies. The main components of the programme
consist of:-
ú Reducing the spread of HIV in groups at high risk by
identification of target populations and providing peer
counselling, condom promotion, and treatment of sexually
transmitted infections.
ú Preventive intervention for the general population by
Information, Education and Communication (IEC) and awareness
campaign, provision of voluntary testing and counselling,
safe blood transfusion services and prevention of
occupational exposure.
ú Providing financial assistance for opportunistic
infections, home and community based care.
ú Strengthening effectiveness and technical, managerial,
financial sustainability of the intervention programmes at
national, State and Community levels.
ú Promoting collaboration amongst public, private and
voluntary sectors.

records.title: TICKETLESS TRAIN TRAVELLERS IN BIHAR .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that majority of train passengers in Bihar 
travel without ticket;
(b) if so, the reasons theerefor;
(c) what steps are being taken to ensure the entry of authorized ticket
holders only in trains, and that the reserved seat passengers are not harassed
by unauthorized passengers; and
(d) the annual revenue loss suffered by the Railways due to ticketless travellers
and the amount collected from the defaulters, in Bihar?
ANSWER
MINISTER O STATE IN THE MINISTRY O PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS AND

MINISTER OF
STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS 
(SHRI O. RAJAGOPAL)
a)and(b): The exact extent of ticketless travel is not quantifiable. however, intensive 
checks have been done over Eastern, North Eastern, Northeast fromtier and South
Eastern Railways, the portions of which are serving the State of Bihar.
(c): In addition to manning of reserved coaches by ticket checking staf, intensive drives 
are regularly conducted by Commercial and Vigilance departments in association with the 
Police against ticketless/irregular travel and also to prevent entry of unauthorized
passengers in reserved compartments. Unauthorized passengers are dealt with 
as per the relevant provisions of law.
(d): Ticket checking on the Railways is a continuous activity. however, the loss 
sufered due to ticketless travellers which go undetectd cannot be assessed.
State-wise figures are not maintined.

children engaged in hazardous domestic and small scale

glass, bidi, etc., are illiterate;
(b) if so, whether Government have drawn any scheme to
make them literate;

(d) if not, the reasons therefor and how Government
propose to make them literate?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT 
(PROF. RITA VERMA)
(a) Separate data is not maintained by this Ministry about
the literacy status of girl children engaged in specific
industries.
(b), (c) & (d) To provide education to child labour, the
Ministry of Labour has been running a programme called the
National Child Labour Project (NCLP). This Ministry has also
launched Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, a national level programme
for Universal Elementary Education which aims to provide
quality elementary education to all children in the 6-14 age
group across the country by the year 2010. The Education
Guarantee Scheme & Alternative and Innovative Education (EGS
& AIE), a component of SSA with effect from the Tenth Plan,
also provides strategies for child labour and adolescent
girls to provide life oriented and gender sensitive
education.

details:
to 
answer to Unstarred Question 191, given in the Rajya Sabha on the 1st March, 2002 and 
state:
(a) what steps have been taken in the new consumption norms for fertilizer industry, to 
minimize reliance on imported fertilizers; and
(b) whether these new norms are expected to move towards self-sufficiency in fertilizers 
and boost their exports; if not, the reasons therefor?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (SHRI S. B. MOOKHERJEE)
(a) and (b): The revision of consumption norms on interim basis w.e.f. 1.4.2000 was 
done in order to fix the consumption norms at the realistic levels, based on the actual 
levels achieved in 1999-2000, or the existing level, whichever is lower. Government 
does not expect any significant fall in production of urea on account of interim revision 
of consumption norms. However, the Government is monitoring the availability vis-à-vis 
demand of urea and will take suitable steps to ensure that there is no significant gap 
between the demand and supply of urea.
If availability of urea happens to be more than the demand, then the Government 
can permit the export of urea.

details:

(a)&(b): Promotion of Section Officers (SOs) in the Central Secretariat Service (CSS) to the grade of Under Secretary (US) have got delayed owing, inter alia, to protracted litigation in the CAT, Principal Bench as well as in the Supreme Court over the issue of inter se seniority of direct recruits and promotee SOs. records.title: PDS RATION TO INCOME TAX PAYEES .
details: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
( SHRI ASHOK PRADHAN )
(a): The stock of foodgrains in the Central pool as on 1st January, 2002 was 580.32 lakh 
tonnes (rice- 256.17 lakh tonnes and wheat - 324.15 lakh tonnes) as against the minimum Buffer 
Stocking norm of 168.00 lakh tonnes of foodgrains including 84 lakh tonnes of rice and 84 lakh
tonnes of wheat.
(b),(c)&(d): Income-tax payers have not been debarred to draw ration from fair price shops
under Public Distribution System (PDS). However, in order to target the PDS towards the poor,
the levy sugar supply under the PDS has been restricted only to the families living below 
poverty line (BPL) in all States/UTs except the North-Eastern States. Hill States and Island
Territories w.e.f. 1.2.2201.
 In view of the abundant stocks of wheat and rice in the central pool, the steps taken by
the Government of India to enhance food security are as under:
i) The entitlement for BPL families was raised from 10 kg per family per month to 20 kg per
family per month from April, 2000 and further to 25 kg per family per month w.e.f. 12.7.2001.
ii) In November, 2000, it was decided to make foodgrains available at CIPs applicable for BPL 
families for all the welfare schemes including SC/ST/OBC hostels, implemented by the various 
Ministries of the Government of India.
iii) In November, 2000, a decision was taken to make foodgrains available at BPL rates for 
allotment to State Governments @ 5 kg. per head per month for covering categories of indigent
people living in welfare institutions, such as beggar homes, orphanages/Nari Niketans, etc; 
sponsored by the State Governments and the concerned administrative Ministry of the Government 
of India.
iv) In November, 2000, another decision was taken to make foodgrains available at BPL rates
for development schemes (where the beneficiaries belong to the BPL category) implemented by
Non-Government Organisations (NGOs), sponsored by the State Governments and endorsed by the 
administrative Ministry in the Government of India, as also by international organizations like
the World Food Programme.
v) On 1.12.2000, the allocation of foodgrains for Below the Poverty Line (BPL) families was
revised on the basis of populations projections of the Registrar General as on 1.3.2000. As a 
result, the number of BPL families eligible for subsidized foodgrains has increased from 
5.96 crores families to 6.52 crore families.
vi) The Antyodaya Anna Yojana was announced on 25.12.2000 for one crore poorest of the poor
BPL families. The scheme is under implementation in all States/UTs. Each of the Antyodaya 
families is given 25 kg. of foodgrains @ Rs. 2 per kg for wheat and Rs. 3 per kg for rice.
vii) In January, 2001, the Food for Work Programme was introduced under which foodgrains are
allocated free of cost to various States by the Ministry of Rural Development. Government of 
India has allocated 38.33 lakh MTs of foodgrains, from January 2001 upto 12.2.2002 for 
undertaking Food for Work programmes in 11 States. Government of India had allocated one lakh
MTs of foodgrains for distribution in the earthquake-affected areas of Gujarat in January 2001.
viii) In May 2001, Government of India decided to give additional allocation of foodgrains at
BPL rates to the drought affected States for distribution to all the drought affected families 
(BPL & APL) @ 20 kg power family per month for a period of three months in the current financial
year. The Government of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra
and Rajasthan have already been allocated additional foodgrains. The Government of Bihar has
been given additional allocation of 1.80 lakh MTs of wheat at BPL rate for flood relief.
ix) In spite of the rise in the economic cost of wheat and rice w.e.f.1.4.2001, the CIP have
not been increased for the BPL category. The CIPs have been retained at Rs. 4.15 per kg for
wheat and Rs. 5.65 per for rice.
x) The Central Issue Price (CIP) of wheat and rice for the APL category has been reduced 
w.e.f. 12.7.2001, which will be valid till 31.3.2002.
 (Rs. per quintal)
 APL 
Wheat 610
Rice 830
xi) The Ministry of Rural Development has launched the Sampoorna Gramin Rozgar Yojana (SGRY)
on 25th September 2001 based on the announcement made by the Prime Minister on 15th August 2001.
Under the programme, it is envisaged to utilize 50 lakh MTs of foodgrains every year. The 
allocation of foodgrains under SGRY upto 28.2.2002 has been 30.82 lakh MTs.
xii) The Open Market Sale Scheme of wheat was continued during the current financial year 
2001-2002. The quantity sold from April 2001 to 15.2.2002 was 37.87 lakh tonnes.

records.title: TERRITORIAL DEMARCATION BETWEEN INDIA AND BANGLADESH .
details:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)
(a) to (c) A statement is placed on the Table of the House. 
Statement referred to in parts (a) to (c) of the reply to Rajya Sabha
Starred Question No.161 for answer on 14.03.2002
(a) to (c) While the survey authorities of the two countries have completed demarcation of over 4000 kms of the India - Bangladesh boundary, they have not been able to resolve differences in demarcation of about 6.5 kms and have referred the matter to the respective Governments. There are also outstanding issues relating to exchange of enclaves and adverse possessions.
2. The Government of India is keen on an early settlement of all boundary-related matters with Bangladesh in accordance with the terms of the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement of 1974. The Governments have agreed to constitute Joint Boundary Working Groups to address all pending matters. The first meeting of the India - Bangladesh Joint Boundary Working Groups on Border Demarcation, and on Enclaves and Adversely Possessed Territories was held in Dhaka from July 2-4, 2001. In the meeting both sides presented their respective positions on these matters in order to facilitate a clear understanding of each others` points of view and to address the issues in a pragmatic and time-bound manner. The subsequent meetings of the Joint Boundary Working Groups could not take place earlier on account of change of Government in Bangladesh viz. the handing over of power to a neutral caretaker Government on 15 July 2001 and holding of General Elections in early October 2001. The dates for the holding of the next meeting of the Joint Boundary Working Groups have been proposed to Bangladesh and their response is awaited. 
3. The ratification of the Land Boundary Agreement would be completed expeditiously on completion of demarcation.

records.title: IMPACT OF CHINA S ENTRY INTO WTO ON INDIAN INDUSTRIES .
details:
( 
(a) whether it is a fact that China has been allowed entry into WTO;
( 
(b)if so, whether Government have analysed its impact on Indian industries particularly electronics, small scale, food and agriculture; and
( 
(c) the steps being taken to absorb the Chinese impact?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY 
( SHRI RAJIV PRATAP RUDY )
(a ) : Yes, Sir. The Fourth Ministerial meeting of WTO held at Doha, Qatar, decided on 10th October, 2001 to accept the accession instruments indicating the terms and conditions of Peoples Republic of China`s Membership in WTO. Subsequently, on 11th November 2001 the Government of PR China accepted the protocol done at Doha. Accordingly, PR China`s accession to WTO will enter into force on 11 December, 2001, one month after the acceptance of protocol by the Government of PR China.
(b) & ( c ) : India has been actively involved in the GATT / WTO accession process of China which started in 1986. A bilateral agreement was signed with China on 22nd February 2000 where tariff and other concessions were agreed to by China with India. There may not be any immediate impact on Indian industries on account of China`s accession to WTO as such, because India and China have already been exchanging Most Favoured Nation (MFN) Treatment and because the concessions had to be given unilaterally by China on entry to WTO and no reciprocal commitments were involved on the part of India or any other WTO Member. The effects of China`s accession to WTO should, therefore, be beneficial to Indian exports since conditions of market access including in respect of tariffs in the Chinese market will significantly improve. The main policy emphasis is to make the Indian industry globally competitive in addition to regular monitoring of imports, particularly consumer goods.

details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(I.D. SWAMI)
(a)to(c): As per available information some Muslim leaders and organisations have raised their voice in favour of Osama Bin Laden and condemned the US-led air-strikes in Afghanistan and expressed the anguish of the Muslim community over these developments. At the same time some eminent moderate Muslim opinion leaders have supported the efforts to root out terrorism in the name of jehad, or otherwise.
 `Public Order` and `Police` are State subjects as per the Constitution of India and hence maintenance of law and order as well as communal harmony are the primary concern of the State Governments. In so far as the Union Government are concerned, the Government have been providing assistance to the State Governments in a variety of ways to tackle the issues causing communal cleavage - both administrative and promotional - in a sustained manner i.e. assistance in improving their policing infrastructure, sending alert messages periodically, sharing intelligence with them, providing Central Para-military Forces including the composite Rapid Action Force on specific request and issuing guidelines from time to time to promote communal harmony.
 The activities of all organisations having a bearing on maintenance of communal harmony are under constant watch of law enforcement agencies and requisite legal action is taken, wherever necessary.

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES, AGRO AND RURAL INDUSTRIES, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING, DEPARTMENT OF PENSIONS AND PENSIONERS WELFARE OF THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENTS OF ATOMIC ENERGY AND SPACE. (SMT.VASUNDHARA RAJE)
(a),(b)&(c): As per the information furnished by the Central Vigilance Commission(CVC), it has set up a virtual organization, named as, Council for a Clean India (CFCI). The Commission have no intention of making it into a registered or a corporate body. Instead, in the website of the CVC, the names of all the participants of CFCI would be included. The Government, however, has not received any formal proposal from the Commission in this regard.
 It is a forum which brings for the first time the officials/agencies concerned with fighting corruption like CVC, CBI, Vigilance Commissioners, Ombudsmen in the Banking and Insurance Sector along with NGOs fighting corruption as well as eminent people concerned with fighting corruption. CFCI is a virtual organization, not formally registered with any agency, it does not have the status of a quasi-judicial authority.

records.title: ILLEGAL BLOOD TRADE .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (SHRI A. RAJA)
(a) There have been isolated incidences of illegal blood trade like operation of unlicensed blood banks and collection of blood from paid donors by private blood banks. There has been no instance of Government Blood Banks indulging in illegal blood trade.
(b) Recently two blood banks at Meerut involved in illegal trade of blood were ordered to stop collection of blood from 14th June, 2001 under the provisions of Drugs & Consmetics Rules and are being prosecuted. Licenses of 5 blood banks in Andhra Pradesh were also withdrawn for not conforming to the norms of Drugs & Cosmetics Rules.
(c) Professional Donation of blood has been banned in the country since 1st January, 1998. For generating enough blood through voluntary blood donation programme, the Government of India have taken a number of steps such as media campaign through TB, AIR and newspapers, developing IEC material for one-to-one communication, observation of National Voluntary Blood Donation day on 1st October every year, encouraging rational use of blood among clinicians and the launching of special campaign to educate masses to support voluntary blood donation. Strict vigilance is being maintained by Drugs Controllers of all States to ensure that no paid donation takes place and no unlicensed blood banks operate.

records.title: INDO NEPAL RELATIONS .
details:
(a) whether Government are apprehensive about the relations between Nepal and India after the situation created by massacre in Royal Palace, Nepal followed by the resignation of their Prime Minister; and
(b) what diplomatic action has been taken to ensure that the existing relations between the two countries improve further?

THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI OMAR ABDULLAH)
(a) and (b)
A Statement is placed on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN PARTS (A) AND (B) OF THE ANSWER TO RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 3428 TO BE ANSWERED ON 23.08.2001 ON `INDO-NEPAL RELATIONS IN THE WAKE OF ROYAL MASSACRE`
In an unfortunate tragic incident, King Birendra and Queen Aishwarya along with some other members of the Royal Family of Nepal were shot dead on June 1, 2001. Crown Prince Dipendra, who was involved in the shoot out, also succumbed to his injuries and died on June 4, 2001. Gyanendra Bir Bikram Shah Dev, younger brother of Late King Biendra, was pronounced the new King by the Royal Council of Nepal and was enthroned on June 4, 2001.
2.. Immediately after the tragic incident, Government of India released a statement which was read out by the External Affairs Minister on June 2. It stated that as a close neighbour and friend, India conveyed its heartfelt condolences to the mourning nation of the Kingdom of Nepal. A three day State mourning was declared by Government of India as a mark of respect. On the same day, the Indian Cabinet passed a Resolution at a specially convened emergency meeting. Rashtrapatiji conveyed his condolences to the new King. PM sent letters of condolence to the Queen Mother and the then PM Girija Prasad Koirala. While expressing condolences, confidence was expressed that friendship and co-operation would continue between our two countries in pursuit of peace and progress and mutually beneficial development.
3. Soon after assumption of office by Hon`ble Sher Bahadur Deuba as the Prime Minister of Nepal, PM spoke to him over the telephone and a congratulatory message was sent thereafter. 
4. The enduring bonds of friendship between India and Nepal are strong and are based on mutual understanding and trust. Our relations have withstood the test of time and Internal developments in one country will not be allowed by either side to adversely affect the other and relations between the two.
5. The existing bilateral mechanisms between the two countries continue to be in operation. Agencies of the two governments are meeting regularly. Some of the Meetings held recently include the Fourth Meeting of the Joint Working Group on Border Management in June, 2001 and the Inter-Governmental Meeting to discuss matters relating to Trade and Transit in August, 2001.
6. The External Affairs Minister, Shri Jaswant Singh, also paid a goodwill visit to Kathmandu from August 17 to 19, 2001. This was the first high level contact between the two governments since the enthronement of King Gyanendra on Jule 4, 2001.

records.title: ENCOURAGEMENT TO SMALL SAVINGS
details:
(a) whether Government considers that small savings have a role 
 to play in the Indian economy;
(b) if so, the reasons for discouraging small savings by its 
 anti-small savings policies such as reduction in the rates of 
 interests on provident funds, NSS, Kisan Vikas Patras, other 
 Post Office Schemes etc.;
(c)whether Government have analysed the impact of the above decisions 
 on the welfare of poor and middle class people in the country; and
(d) if so, the results thereof and what steps are being proposed/
 being taken to encourage small savings and make small savings 
 attractive ?

( )MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
( )SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL
(a)to(d) Savings play a very important role in the economy of the 
country. The decision to rationalise interest rates on 
small savings schemes has been taken as the real rates 
of interest were considered to be high preventing downward
movement of other rates of interest in the economy. A lower 
interest structure is expected to stimulate growth from 
which all sections of the society would benefit. Steps are
taken by the Government from time to time to safeguard the 
interests of the small investors by ensuring attractive
returns, tax benefits, liquidity & accessibility.

records.title: COLLAPSE OF CIVIL AND CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM .
details:
MINISTER OF LAW, JUSTICE AND COMPANY AFFAIRS AND SHIPPING (SHRI ARUN JAITLEY) (a): No, Sir.
As per information made available by the National Crime Records Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs, the average conviction rate of crimes under the Indian Penal Code from the year 1995 to 1999 has been 39.02%. 
(b): The reasons for poor conviction rate, inter alia, can be attributed to the nature of the procedural laws, practices and procedures followed by criminal courts and the inadequencies of the investigating and prosecuting agencies. 
(c) to (e) :Various steps have been taken by the Government for the speedy disposal of both civil and criminal cases. These include amendment of the Civil Procedure Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure, increase in the number of posts of Judges/Judicial Officers, establishment of Special Courts/tribunals, computerisation of courts and adoption of alternative modes of dispute resolution, such as, arbitration and conciliation. Lok Adalats have been given a statutory base as supplementary forum for resolution of disputes.
As regards Criminal Procedure Code, the Law Commission of India has comprehensively reviewed the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973. The Government has recently appointed a Committee under the chairmanship of Shri Justice V.S.Malimath, to
suggest measures for revamping the Criminal Justice System. 
Government has sanctioned a scheme involving an amount of Rs.502.90 crore for creation of 1734 Fast Track Courts for expeditious disposal of long pending sessions cases and cases involving undertrials in jails, on priority. The scheme is in operation with effect from April, 2001.

records.title: PAUCITY OF SPACE IN THE VAULTS OF NATIONALISED BANKS IN JAIPUR
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that nationalised banks in Jaipur are finding it difficult to accept currency deposits owing to paucity of space in their vaults; and 
(b) if so, what steps are being taken to transfer the accumulated currency to Reserve Bank of India or other sources to facilitate the depositors for their deposits in the banks?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL)
(a):- Yes, Sir.
(b) :- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has taken following steps in this regard :
a) Short Term Measures
i) Notes are regularly lifted from the currency chests in Jaipur.
ii) Diversion orders have been issued from Jaipur to Bhopal, Mumbai and Nagpur to ease the pressure on Jaipur Office.
iii) In order to dispose of soiled notes at RBI expeditiously, RBI has opened one New Note Examination Hall (Revised Procedure) which disposes of the soiled ntes 150% of the Normal Procedure. RBI has also introduced 2 Modified Procedure Section to dispose of lower denominations notes at fast track which disposes of soiled notes 200% the Normal Procedure.
b) Long Term Measures
RBI is introducing Currency Verification and Processing Systems at Jaipur Office shortly which will dispose of soiled notes at 50,000 pieces per hour. Thus, the soiled notes from nationalized banks are periodically taken over by RBI, Jaipur for processing and disposal.

details:
(a) whether it is a fact that the quantity of RSPM, Nitrogen Dioxide and Sulphur in the atmosphere over Delhi has been over the safe level for the last many days;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps being taken to reduce their level which otherwise may tell upon the health of people living in the National Capital?
ANSWER
MINISTER OF ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS
(SHRI T.R. BAALU)
(a), 
(b) & 
(c) A statement is laid on the Table of the House.
STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS 
(a), 
(b) & 
(c) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 288 FOR 10.8.2001 REGARDING `POLLUTANTS LEVEL IN DELHI` RAISED BY SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
________________________________________________________________
(a) & 
(b) The ambient air quality is being monitored at seven locations in Delhi. During July-August, 2001, the average levels of Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM), Oxides of Nitrogen and Sulphur dioxide in Delhi have been reported by Central Pollution Control Board to be below their safe limits. However, the prescribed limits of Respirable Suspended Particulate Matter (RSPM) and Oxides of Nitrogen were exceeded on a few days at a few locations mainly due to vehicular emissions.
(c) The steps taken to control pollution include the following:-
(i) Action Plan to control pollution in Delhi has been prepared and is being implemented.
(ii) Emission standards for on-road vehicles and mass emission standards for new vehicles have been notified under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and are enforced by Transport Departments of the State Governments including Delhi.
(iii) A comprehensive Policy for Abatement of Pollution that lays stress on both the control and preventive aspects of pollution has been formulated.
(iv) Unleaded petrol is supplied in the entire country from 1.2.2000 and diesel with 0.25% sulphur maximum content is supplied from 1.1.2000 in the entire country. Ultra low sulphur (0.05%) fuel (petrol and diesel) has also been introduced in major cities.
(v) Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) is supplied for automobiles through a number of retail outlets in Delhi to cater to the CNG vehicles. 
(vi) Benzene concentration in petrol has been reduced. 
(vii) A network of 290 Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations has been set up throughout the country.
(viii) Emission standards for industries have been notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to check pollution.
(ix) Industries are also required to install necessary pollution control equipments before commissioning of their plants.
(x) Industries are required to take consent from the respective State Pollution Control Board under the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.
****

details:

people affected by floods in Orissa, in time;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the rescue operations started with the help of army could 
provide relief only to 40 per cent of the flood victims;
(c) what are the reasons for the civil authorities not acting in alacrity to provide timely relief 
to the flood affected people; and
(d) whether any probe is proposed to be undertaken in this regard?

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE 
(SHRI SHRIPAD Y. NAIK)
(a) to (d): Distribution of relief at the ground level is the responsibility of the State 
Government. The Government of Orissa had reportedly taken all necessary steps from the 
beginning including issuing timely warnings, instructions to the District Collectors for 
evacuation of people and arranging relief supplies to the affected people. The State 
Government have informed that food stocks were available and that the sarpanches were 
authorised to administer relief in most cases. According to the State Government, the 
marooned people were rescued by the civilian authorities and the army and about 7 lakh 
people were evacuated during different stages of flood.
The State Government have also informed that the civil authorities have provided relief 
in time and that no probe is being undertaken.

details:

Information from the neighbouring States is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.
(b): Between 11.4.2001 to 17.5.2001, 75 ULFA militants were nabbed by the security forces. 19 ULFA militants died in various encounters with the security forces in the said period.
(c)&(d): There has been no failure of intelligence and security forces in Assam in containing the violence unleashed by the militants. The Government has taken various steps to protect lives and properties from terrorist outfits in Assam. This include, inter-alia, deployment of Para-military Forces and Army in the State, coordinated action by Army, Para-military Forces and State Police for counter insurgency operations, declaration of major insurgent groups as unlawful associations under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967; declaration of the entire State of Assam as `disturbed area` under the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958; reimbursement of security related expenditure to the State Government and modernization/up-gradation of State Police Force. Regular review of the situation both at State and Central Government level is being made.
 Following effective security arrangements, 74.38% voters were able to cast their vote in the General Assembly Elections held in May, 2001 in Assam.

records.title: . . PROTECTION OF TIGERS
details:
MINISTER FOR ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS (SHRI T.R.BAALU)
(a) & (b) As against 1827 tigers in 1972, India now has about 3800 tigers. 
(c) The number of deaths of tigers during last two years is as follows:
 1999 2000
Natural death 16 15
Death due to poaching 38 39
Total 54 54
(d) Action against the poachers is invariably taken by the State Governments. As such the list of poachers is not compiled and collated by the Government of India. However the list of important cases and poachers arrested is given in Annexure 1.
(e) The details are given in Annexure II.
ANNEXURE I
ANNEXURE IN RESPECT OF PART (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED 
QUESTION NO. 1422 TO BE ANSWERED ON 03-08-2001 REGARDING 
`PROTECTION OF TIGERS`
Details of offenders arrested and action taken 
i. On 18.12.99, 3 tiger skins, 50 leopard skins and 5 otter skins were seized at Sahibabad, 
Uttar Pradesh border. 8 nos. of offenders were arrested. The investigation has been 
completed and the complaint has been filed in the court.
ii. On 12.1.2000, 4 nos. of tiger skins, 70nos. of leopard skins,18000nos. of leopard claws, 
132 nos. of tiger claws and 221 nos. of black buck skins were seized at Khaga. 6 nos. 
offenders were arrested. The investigation has been completed and the complaint 
has been filed in the court.
iii. On 15.1.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 2 persons for 
possessing 1 tiger and 1 leopard skin at Atariya Railway Station, Sitapur. Investigation is 
in progress.
iv. On 6.2.2001 one tiger carcass was found in Nallamala forests in Andhra Pradesh. 5 
offenders were arrested. Investigation is under progress.
v. On 25.2.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 4 persons for illegal possession 
of 1 tiger skin, 41 kgs of bones including 7 tiger skulls at Kheri (Palia). Investigation is i
n progress.
vi. On 21.3.2001, 1 tiger skin, 5 tiger skulls, 1.9 kgs antler horns, 10 nos. of tiger claws, 23 kgs 
of tiger bones, 3 nos. of tiger teeth and 4 nos. of leopard skins were seized by Central 
Bureau of Investigation in Nagpur. 6 nos. of offenders were arrested. The investigation 
is in progress.
vii. On 7.4.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 3 persons for illegal possession 
of 1 tiger skin and 1 leopard skin at Palia, Kheri. Investigation in progress.
viii. On 27.4.2001, the Special Task Force, ttar Pradesh arrested 5 persons for possessing 1 tiger 
and 19 leopard skin at Kanpur and 5 leopard skin and 10 claws in Lucknow. Investigation is 
in progress.
ix. On 14.5.2001, the Special Task Force, Uttar Pradesh arrested 2 persons for possessing 2 
suspected tiger skin at Allahabad. Investigation is in progress.
ANNEXURE II
ANNEXURE IN RESPECT OF PART (e) OF THE RAJYA SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION
NO. 1422 TO BE ANSWERED ON 03-08-2001 REGARDING `PROTECTION OF TIGERS`. 
STEPS TAKEN BY THE GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
NATIONAL LEVEL
1. Setting up of a National Coordination Committee to control poaching and illegal 
trade in wildlife with enforcement agencies like customs, Revenue Intelligence, 
Indo-Tibetan Border Police, Border Security Force, Central Reserves Police, Coast Guards,
 State Police, Deputy Director, Wildlife Preservation & Scientific Organisation like 
Zoological and Botanical Survey of India. 
2. Training Programs and Workshops have been organised to sensitize the above departments
to be proactive in control of trade and smuggling of wildlife products. 
3. A special co-ordination committee with Secretary (E&F), Special Secretary (Home),
 Director, CBI and representative of the Chairman, central Board of Excise & Customs has 
been created to ensure better co-ordination in the efforts to curb smuggling of wildlife products. 
4. Central assistance is being provided to State Governments to strengthen the protection 
infrastructure including armed squads, vehicles, communication network and co-ordination 
between the Park Managers. 
5. Schemes for awards and rewards for outstanding performance and acts of valor has been 
introduced to encourage detection and reporting.
6. The State Government have been advised to strengthen vigilance and intensify patrolling. 
7 Launching of public awareness programme to involve Non-Governmental Organisations and 
others for supporting the Government in its efforts towards wildlife conservation. 
8. Supporting programmers of Institutions and NGOs in exploring tiger-trade routes and developing a forensic identification reference Manual for tiger parts and products. 
9. Funds are being provided to the States Governments for eco-development of the areas to 
reduce the biotic pressure thereon.10. Site specific special force in Project Tiger Areas.
11. Special Strike Force all over the Country to control Trade.
12. Creation of wildlife trade control bureau.
INTERNATIONAL LEVEL :
1. Initiated creation of a Forum of Tiger Range Countries, i.e Global Forum for 
addressing international issues related of tiger conservation. 
2. To control transboundary trade and effect mutual cooperation in tiger conservation:-
(i) A protocol has been signed with People`s Republic of China. 
(ii) An MOU with his Majesty`s Government of Nepal has been signed. 
(iii) Dialogue with Bangladesh has been initiated.
3. Several resolutions at CITES to check illegal trade in Tiger parts and products 
have been adopted at India`s initiative. 
4. The Millennium Tiger Conference was held in March, 1999. The conference declaration 
suggested several action for conservation of tiger both at national and International level.

(a) to (c): The Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) submitted an application on 31.1.2001 seeking approval and financial assistance of Government for holding the 15th Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship at New Delhi from 14th to 20th April, 2001. Thereafter, on 13.2.2001, the Federation indicated that Pakistan and Fiji are not participating in this Championship. Accordingly, after obtaining the clearance of Ministry of External Affairs and Ministry of Home Affairs, permission was given to TTFI for holding the event from 14th to 20th April, 2001. Later on, the Table Tennis Federation informed on 22.3.2001 that Pakistan has confirmed its participation. As such after obtaining the clearance of Ministry of External Affairs, the approval for inviting the Table Tennis Team of Pakistan was conveyed on 11th April, 2001. As such, it will be seen that there has been no delay on the part of the Government of India in giving clearance to the participation of Pakistan Table Tennis Team in the 15th Com monwealth Table Tennis Championship.
 There is no basis for linking Pakistan`s non-participation in the 15th Commonwealth Table Tennis Championship with India`s decision not to play in Sharjah. India`s decision for not playing in Sharjah Cricket tournament is based on a policy decision taken by the Government of India not to play any cricket matches at non-regular Cricket venues at least for a period of three years.

records.title: DEMOLITION OF STATUES BUDDHA .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI U. V. KRISHNAM RAJU)
(a)-(b) Following the issue of a decree on 26th February, 2001 ordering the destruction of all statues in Afghanistan, appeals were addressed internationally to the Taliban not to destroy historical works of art, being the heritage of all mankind. The Buddha Statues at Bamiyan were specifically mentioned. The Taliban militia completely disregarded international opinion and appeals and carried out this act of cultural vandalism over a period of time.
In a statement issued on 27th February, 2001, the Government condemned the Taliban decree and called upon them to ensure full protection of Bamiyan Buddhas and all other relics. On 2nd March, 2001, the External Affairs Minister made a statement in both Houses of Parliament in which he, inter-alia, offered to bring these artifacts to India for safekeeping for the Afghan people. On the same day both Houses of Parliament adopted unanimous resolutions condemning this barbarism. 
The Government also raised this issue internationally. Prime Minister wrote to several Heads of Governments, including the permanent members of the UN Security Council, the UN Secretary General and to Heads of Governments of countries with Buddhist populations (Bhutan, Japan, Sri Lanka, Lao People`s Democratic Republic, Mongolia, Thialand, Cambodia, Myanmar, Republic of Korea) urging that the collective voice of humanity be raised against this outrage and that the Taliban be made to see reason. India co-sponsored a UNGA resolution adopted on 9th March, 2001 on the destruction of Bamiyan Buddhas and other manifestations of Afghanistan`s pre-Islamic art. The Resolution called upon the Taliban to abide by their previous commitments to protect Afghanistan`s cultural heritage from all acts of vandalism damage and theft.
There was widespread international condemnation of the Taliban militia`s actions. The UN Secretary General, Director General of UNESCO, European Union and several Muslim countries were severely critical of the Taliban militia. During Prime Minister`s recent visit to Iran, the President of the Islamic Republic of Iran while condemning the Taliban actions said that they had brought a bad name to Islam.
(c)-(d) The Government is aware of harsh discriminatory policies of the Taliban against the minorities and their places of worship in Afghanistan. Government has brought this to the attention of its foreign interlocutors.

details:

BY
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)
(a) and (b) One Indian doctor, Dr. Mona Verma, who was practising in the State of Queensland, Australia during the period from September 1998 to December 1999 has alleged harassment and acts of racism. The complaints centered around (1) alleged pressure on her by her Australian employer to commit unethical practices such as administering psychotropic substances and false certification of insanity (2) denial by the Medical Board of Queensland of registration despite her possessing the requisite sponsorship from another employer; and (3) refusal by the Australian High Commission of a `bridging visa` to return to Australia. MEA had pressed her case with the Australian High Commission in Delhi who regretted that rules do not permit bridging visa to be issued outside Australia. Our High Commission in Canberra had contacted the Queensland Medical Board regarding her complaint of harassment and was asked for an authorisation letter from the doctor. Accordingly we requested Dr. Verma to send us an authorisation letter to enable the High Commission to pursue the enquiries on her behalf with the Queensland Medical Board, but she has not until now sent it.

records.title: DISINVESTMENT OF HINDUSTAN ZINC LTD.
details:
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE DEPARTMENT OF DISINVESTMENT, MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRIES OF PLANNING, STATISTICS & PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS AND PUBLIC GRIEVANCES (SHRI ARUN SHOURIE) 
(a) Yes, Sir.
(b) Government has decided for disinvestment of 26% equity in Hindustan Zinc Ltd. through strategic sale with giving appropriate role in management to the strategic partner. 
(c) & (d) Although the general procedure of sale of equity through strategic sale remains broadly the same, the pattern followed for disinvestment in BALCO can not be replicated in case of disinvestment in Hindustan Zinc Ltd. for various reasons like the following:-
· BALCO was a 100% Government held company and therefore 51% equity could be sold to the strategic partner while retaining 49%. In case of HZL Government holds only 75.92% of the paid-up capital of the company while balance is held by the financial institutions and public. 
· BALCO was not a public listed company but HZL is a public listed company and the shares of the company are traded on Bombay Stock Exchange. The acquirer of the strategic stake offered by the Government would be required to make an open offer for acquiring further shares from other shareholders in accordance with the SEBI take over code. Such a stipulation was not required in case of BALCO since it was not listed on stock exchanges. 
Therefore, different transactions can not be completed in identical manner since the facts and circumstances of every transaction like percentage of equity offered, the quality and number of interested parties, terms and conditions of sale, financial performance of the concerned companies, future prospects of the business of the company are different. The process of disinvestment and the policy of disinvestment are improved / streamlined with the experience gained over time. The experience of disinvestment in BALCO will be useful in the disinvestment of HZL.

 ferred to in parts (a) to (d) of the Rajya Sabha

N.B. Excluding Bagdigi Disaster on 2-2-2001 in which 29

The details of each mishap with particulars of
deceased, causes, management officials held responsible
and compensation paid are given as Annexure-1. However,
the details of Bagdigi Disaster, which took place on 2-2-
2001, are given below.
On 2-2-2001 at about 12.30 P.M. 30 miners including
Manager & One Asstt. Manager were trapped due to sudden
inrush of water in the workings of Bagdigi Colliery. Out
of 30 persons, 29 bodies have been recovered and one
person Shri Salim Ansari was rescued alive from Bagdigi.
While the development of 7 seam in Bagdigi Colliery under
Lodna Area was in progress within the leasehold area of
Bagdigi towards Joyrampur Colliery, Level-III heading of
7 seam of Bagdigi Colliery joined with 15 level
waterlogged old working of Joyrampur Colliery resulting
in inundation of developed galleries of 7 seam of Bagdigi
Colliery. Consequently 30 workers were trapped inside
the mine. The reasons of the mishap will be known after
the statutory enquiry by DGMS and the Court of Enquiry
are submitted.
Pending detailed investigation, the Agent of Bagdigi
Colliery, Shri A.K. Sengupta, the former Surveyor, Shri
R.N. Kundu, and the present Surveyor, Shri R.C. Das had
been put under suspension. General Manager of the mine
has also been transferred. The details of compensation
paid to the families is at Annexure—II.
Steps taken to prevent such mishap
1. Instructions have been issued in writing to all
CGM/GM of the areas that in case of coal extraction
within 60 meters from water logged working in same seam
or in overlying or underlying seams with the approval
DGMS, the conditions stipulated by DGMS to be followed
strictly.
2. A committee consisting of senior officers has been
constituted in each area who will inspect the mines of other
area to ascertain the danger to the working districts and
other workings of the mines due to inundation from surface
as well as underground waters from the different areas of
the same mine or of the neighboring mines and also to
ascertain the danger of influx of
2
noxious/ toxic gasses as well as fire damp into the
working districts or other workings either from the
sealed off area of the same mine or of the other mines.
3. Old workings, isolations and fire stopping are being
inspected as per CMR.
4. Great emphasis has been given for quality inspection
of the mines.
5. Safety Committee meeting at mine level has been made
more effective.
6. To inculcate safety consciousness among workers by
organizing safety week, safety drives, publicity and
propaganda on safety.
7 Extensive training programme has been arranged to
train workers, supervisory staff and executives.
8. Each Area General Manager holds a special safety
meeting on last Friday of the month where they discuss
only about the safety matters.
9. Three outside experts had been appointed to conduct
3rd Round of Safety Audit to examine all aspects of
safety in depth including existing provisions and
recommend precautions and had submitted their reports,
which have been circulated to all collieries and areas
for implementation.
10. Safety First Report of all mines are examined in
every month and suitable measures are taken to secure
safety.

records.title: AGREEMENTS SIGNED WITH CHINA .
details:
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS 
(SHRI JASWANT SINGH)
(a)-(c): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
STATEMENT TO BE PLACED ON THE TABLE OF THE HOUSE WITH REFERENCE TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.183 FOR ANSWER ON MARCH 8, 2001
Agreements signed with China
 Mr. Li Peng, a senior Chinese leader and Chairman of the National Peoples` Congress(NPC) paid an eight-day official visit to India from 9-17 January, 2001 at the joint invitation of the Hon`ble Chairman, Rajya Sabha and the Hon`ble Speaker, Lok Sabha. The visit took place at Chinese request. Mr. Li Peng is the seniormost Chinese leader to visit India since the visit of President Jiang Zemin in November, 1996. This is his second visit. He had visited India in December, 1991 as the Premier of the State Council of China. 
2. During this visit he called on the President, Vice President and Prime Minister. He also held discussions with the Hon`ble Speaker, Deputy Chairperson Rajya Sabha, EAM, Leader of the Opposition, leaders of Parliamentary Groups and Indian Industry. In addition to New Delhi, Mr. Li Peng visited Mumbai, Agra, Bangalore and Hyderabad. 
3. Mr. Li Peng had frank and cordial discussions with our leadership on bilateral relations. He described the primary objective of his visit as the promotion of friendship and cooperation with India. He also said that:
- China places emphasis on maintaining good-neighbourly relations with India. 
- China does not pose a threat to its neighbours. 
- China does not view India as a threat. 
- China wishes to see a prosperous, developed and strong India and welcomes a more active role by India in regional and international affairs. 
- China desires to expand trade and economic cooperation with India. 
- there was need to enhance mutual trust and understanding so that the relationship is based on strong foundations. 
- that the common ground between our two countries far outweighs the differences, and that unresolved problems in our relations should not become impediments to the expansion of our relationship.
4. Prime Minister and other leaders reiterated Government`s commitment to developing friendly and good-neighbourly relations with China on the basis of Panchsheel and mutual sensitivity to each other`s concerns. We welcomed the progress in our bilateral relations and conveyed that interaction should increase and be accelerated. Government believes that as neighbours, India and China have to solve all problems in a reasonable manner to the satisfaction of both countries. This was conveyed to Mr. Li Peng. 
5. The boundary question was discussed in broad terms. In November, 2000 India and China exchanged maps depicting each other`s perceptions of the Line of Actual Control in the Middle Sector of the India-China boundary. This was the first step in the process of clarifying and confirming the LAC along the entire border. During discussions with Mr. Li Peng, it was agreed that the recent development represented progress and marked a good beginning. We have proposed that this process of LAC clarification should be expedited. It has been agreed that the modalities will be discussed in the mechanisms already set up for this purpose. 
6. Our concerns regarding international and cross border terrorism were conveyed to Mr. Li Peng. He said that China condemns international terrorism in all forms.
7 We exchanged views on the international situation in general. There was agreement on the need to develop the international situation towards its natural trend of multi-polarity. 
8. Mr. Li Peng said that cooperation between India and China will benefit peace and stability in the region and the world.
9. It has been agreed to establish Parliamentary Friendship Groups in both Parliaments. 
10. No specific bilateral agreement was signed during the visit.
11. Both sides expressed the desire to enhance trade and economic cooperation. (During the year 2000, bilateral trade, according to Chinese statistics, increased to US$ 2.92 billion, an increase of approximately 47%. India`s exports grew by over 63% and China`s exports by 35%.)
12. Government has already invited Chinese Premier Mr. Zhu Rongji to visit India at a mutually convenient date. Mr. Li Peng extended invitations to Vice President, Prime Minister and Hon`ble Speaker Lok Sabha to visit China. 
13. Government have consistently viewed bilateral relations with China in a positive spirit. Our approach has been principled and based on the premise that good-neighbourly relations are to mutual benefit. The high-level dialogue with China has led to an overall improvement in our bilateral relationship. We believe that our two countries must solve all problems through dialogue in a fair and reasonable manner to the satisfaction of both countries, and with due sensitivity to each other`s concerns.

records.title: BRINGING THE STATE SERVICE COMMISSIONS UNDER PURIVIEW OF UPSC .
details:
(a) whether Government are considering to bring all State
Service Commissions under the purview of UPSC to ensure uniform
standard of examination/selection for similar posts throughout
the country;
(b) if not, whether Government would give a thought to this;
and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

MINISTER OF STATE OF DEPARTMENT OF PERSONNEL AND TRAINING AND
DEPARTMENT OF PENSION AND PENSIONERS` WELFARE IN THE MINISTRY OF
PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SMT. VASUNDHARA RAJE) 
(a) & (b) : No, Sir.
(c) : The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is a
constitutional body entrusted with the duties of conducting
examinations for recruitment to services of the Union under
Article 320 of the Constitution. Under the same Article of the
Constitution, the State Public Service Commissions have been
constituted for conducting examinations for recruitment to
services of the respective States. As the State public services
and the State Public Service Commissions are included in the
State List in the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India
and Union Public services and the Union Public Service Commission
finds place in the Union List of the said Schedule, it is neither
possible nor desirable to bring the State Public Service
Commissions under the purview of UPSC.

records.title: USE OF NON CONVENTIONAL SOURCES OF ENERGY IN INDUSTRIAL UNITS .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE FOR NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY SOURCES 
(INDEPENDENT CHARGE) (SHRI M. KANNAPPAN)
(a): All the thirteen States, which have metropolitan cities, except the State of West Bengal, have reported shortage of power supply ranging from 1.6% to 13.3%.
(b): No, Sir. The total installed capacity of projects for generation of power from non-conventional sources at present is less than 3% of the overall installed capacity of power generation in our country. It is, therefore, not considered appropriate to compulsorily substitute the conventional power for any industrial units with power from non-conventional sources. 
(c): The Ministry is implementing a wide range of centrally sponsored schemes / programmes to maximise the use of non-conventional energy sources by providing various fiscal, financial and promotional incentives to promoters, entrepreneurs, beneficiaries, implementing agencies / organizations, State Electricity Boards, etc. In 
addition, higher subsidies / incentives are provided under major programmes to special 
category of people such as Schedule Castes and Schedule Tribes as well as in specific areas such as North-East States, Hilly areas, Islands, etc. Programmes, which are especially suited for metropolitan cities include: solar photovoltaic and solar thermal applications, recovery of energy from urban wastes and solar passive architecture. 
(d): The achievements made during the last three years in the country in respect of non-conventional source of energy are given in the Annexure. As regards the targets for the next three years, these are fixed on year to year basis and are in accordance with approved Annual Plans and Five Year Plan.

records.title: IMPORT OF PALM OIL .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that palm oil is continued to be imported 
despite his Ministry`s decision to ban its import;
(b) if so, the reasons therefore;
(c) what steps have been taken to protect the interest of local
 producers and to encourage them for self-sufficiency; and
(d) how much foreign exchange has been spent during the last three 
years on the import of palm oil?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION ( SHRI V. SREENIVASA PRASAD )
(a) & (b) : As per EXIM Policy, import of edible oils except coconut 
oil, which is canalised, is on OGL. In other words, all edible oils except
coconut oil are freely importable.
(c) Some of the measures taken to protect the interest of the local 
producers and to encourage them for self-sufficiency are -
(i) W.e.f. 21.11.2000, the duty on import of edible oils has been
raised, for edible grade crude vegetable oil from 25% (basic) to 35% and
for refined vegetable oils from 35% (basic) to 45% (basic). In case of 
RBD palmolein and other palm oil products, the duty has been raised from 35% 
(basic) to 65% (basic). Even the duty on edible grade CPO and its 
fractions for the manufacture of vanaspati has been raised from 15% to 25%.
(ii) Concessional rate of duty has been allowed only to processors for
captive consumption.
(iii) Use of domestically grown oils in the manufacture of vanaspati to
a minimum of 25% oil-mix has been made compulsory.
(d) Import of edible oils being on OGL, precise figures about the 
foreign exchange spent by the private Trade and Industry are not available.
However, the foreign exchange spent by the State Trading Corporation (STC)
which is importing on Government account has been as under:

details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(I.D. SWAMI)
(a) & (b): The recent killings of innocent civilians in Assam are mainly due to the desperation of ULFA as it has been losing support from the public in Assam and its cadres are demoralized.
 There are reports of collaboration between ULFA and other militant groups.

Regular review of the situation both at State and Central Government level is being made.

records.title: DISTURBANCE IN KASHMIR BY PAK PRISONERS .
details:
(a) whether Government are aware that the Pakistan Government is reported to have assured freedom to its prisoners on contract for killing and creating disturbances in Kashmir; and 
(b) if so, the steps proposed to be undertaken to counter such a move?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(CH. VIDYASAGAR RAO)
(a): Yes Sir. Pakistan and Pakistan sponsored terrorist groups have been continuously attempting to induct foreign mercenaries from across the border/LoC into J&K for continuing the ongoing terrorism. Such mercenaries have also included criminals, smugglers and ex-servicemen as well as impressionable youth.
(b): With a view to deal with the cross border terrorism the Government has adopted a multi pronged approach which includes, inter-alia, strengthening the border management, neutralising plans of the militants by appropriate action against them in the hinterland, gearing up intelligence machinery, greater functional framework of operation Groups and Intelligence Groups of the UHQ at all levels, improved technology, weapons and equipments for Security Forces, closer vigil on the border, establishment of more naka parties in depth areas to check infiltration/exfiltration, more police pickets, intensive patrolling etc.

records.title: SELF SUFFICIENCY IN CRUDE PRODUCTION .
details:
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRYOF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS 
(SHRI E. PONNUSWAMY)
- 
(a): & (b): The target set for the crude oil production during 2000-01 is 32.46 Million Metric Tonne (MMT) including additional 0.5 MMT production planned by ONGC and the actual production in the first seven month (April-Oct., 2000) has been 18.94 MMT (Provisional).
The indigenous production during 2001-02 is estimated to be about 32.30 MMT. The production for the subsequent 2-3 years would have been of a similar magnitude; however various measures taken by the Government as given in reply to part (c) are expected to increase the production.
The demand for crude oil for the year 2004-05 would be worked out as a part of the Xth Plan preparation, the exercise of which is yet to commence. 
(c): Government has taken several steps to increase crude oil production in the country, which include:-
i) To improve the recovery factor from existing major fields by implementing Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR)/Improved Oil Recovery (IOR) schemes. These would also help in accelerating oil production from the fields.
ii) To add reserves by exploring in the deeper layers in the producing areas.

(a) : During the period November, 1999 to October, 2000,

(b): These flights are delayed mostly due to adversfe
weather airport restrictions, technical snags, and
miscellaneous and consequential reasons. 
(c): Air India has taken several steps to ensure their
operation as per schedule such as 
(i) all delays are
investigated to pinpoint the cause and remedial action is
taken wherever necessary;

continuously monitored and the processes/procedures/systems
are constantly evaluated, reviewed and upgraded; 
(iii) Air
India`s Delay Monitoring Committee meets every day and
fortnightly meeting is also conducted with the officers of
DGCA to analyse every delay and take preventive actions; 
(iv) Air India`s Technical Cell plans for repair action on
aircraft which are know to be coming with a snag. This Cell
also looks into the snag which occurs at outstations; 
(v)
periodic refresher training is conducted for Air India`s
engineers and technicians.

records.title: EMPLOYMENT OF PERSONNEL IN PRIVATE SECTOR
details:
(a) whether there exists a mechanism to ascertain employment
of personnel in private sector;
(b) if so, how many cases of violation of minimum wages have
to come to light; and
(c) the action taken against the defaulters?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT ( SHRI MUNI LALL )
- - 
(a): The National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) collects
data on employment through comprehensive surveys on quinquennial
basis. In addition to the quinquennial surveys, NSSO also
conducts annual surveys with a smaller sample size. Besides, the
Directorate General of Employment & Training also collects data
on employment in the organised sector under its Employment Market
Information (EMI) Programme.
(b) & (c): As regards violation of minimum wages, the
enforcement of the provisions of Minimum Wages Act, 1948 is
secured through the officers of Central Industrial Relations
Machinery in the Central sphere. In the State sphere, the
enforcement is secured through the State Enforcement Machinery.
The officers who conduct regular inspections, take appropriate
action whenever any case of non-payment or less payment of
minimum wages is detected.
 In the Central sphere, most of the mines covered as
scheduled employment under the Minimum Wages Act are in private
sector. As per the latest available information pertaining to
violations of the provisions of the Minimum Wages Act in mines in
Central sphere during 1998-99 as many as 3671 inspections were
carried out in which 44806 irregularities were detected, 1547
employers convicted, 394 claim cases disposed of and an amount of
Rs. 38.45 lakhs awarded.

records.title: PROCEDURE TO DEBAR THE INCOME TAX PAYERS FROM PDS .
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that those who paid income tax for 1999-2000 have been denied ration
from PDS shops w.e.f. 1st July, 2000; 
(b) if so, whether among those who are not required to pay income tax on their income for
 the year 2000-2001 will automatically become entitled for ration from PDS shops; and
(c) what is the procedure adopted in such cases?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
( SHRI SRIRAM CHAUHAN )
(a), (b) & (c) : The Government has not debarred the Income Tax payers from the purview
of the Public distribution System (PDS) for supply of foodgrains, edible oils and kerosene. 
The Government of India have decided to exclude Income Tax Assesses and their family members 
from the purview of PDS sugar from July, 2000 onwards. Accordingly pending finalisation of the 
list of income tax assesses and their family members with the help of income tax authorities,
ad-hoc reduction in the monthly levy sugar quota of States/UTs has been made.
 The State Governments have been advised to obtain a simple declaration from the ration 
card holders as to whether or not he/she and his/her family members is/are income tax assesses.
Such declaration has a provision that in the event the declaration made is found, on 
verification, to be false, the cardholder is liable for cancellation of his/her card or such 
other penalty as the State Government may decide to impose.

records.title: BANGLADESHIS IN INDIA .
details:
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
( I.D. SWAMY)
(a) & (b) : In view of the long and porous border with Bangladesh and also on account of various push and pull factors, many Bangladeshis have managed to sneak into various parts of the country. It is difficult to make a realistic estimate of the number of illegal immigrants from Bangladesh because they enter surreptitiously and are able to mingle easily with the local population due to ethnic and linguistic similarities.
( c) The powers of detection and deportation of foreigners have been delegated to the State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations, under Section 3 (2) ( c) of the Foreigners Act, 1946. Instructions have been issued to the State Governments/ Union Territory Administrations to intensify efforts to identity and deport illegal foreign nationals and also to sensitise the local population about the magnitude and seriousness of the problem. There is no proposal at present to issue identity cards to Bangladeshi nationals. 
2/-
-2-
(d) A series of measures have been taken by the Government to curb the problem of infiltration of Bangladeshi nationals into India. These include raising of additional Battalions of Border Security Force. Reduction of gaps between the border outposts, intensification of patrolling both on the land and the riverine border, accelerated programme of construction of border roads and fencing, increase in the number of outpost towers, provision of surveillance equipments etc . The matter has also been taken up with the Government of Bangladesh on various occasions. The progress of these measures is reviewed regularly. State Governments and Union Territory Administrations have also been directed to enforce the provisions of the Foreigners Act, 1946 (IMDT Act 1983 in case of Assam) strictly.
