records.title: TERM LOAN TO MNCS FOR ACQUISITION OF ASSETS
details:
(a) whether the acquisition of cement plants by Foreign
 Multi-Nationals in India is through funds received
 from abroad;
(b) whether Indian Financial Institutions and Banks are
 extending funds as Term Loan or Working Capital for
 such acquisition; and
(c) what is the policy of Government in respect of
 encouraging Indian Financial Institutions and Banks to
 extend Term loan to Multi-Nationals for acquisition of
 existing Indian assets?

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE SHRI V. DHANANJAY
KUMAR
MINISTRY OF FINANCE
(a),(b)&(c): Foreign investors, including foreign
companies, are allowed to establish companies in India after
obtaining requisite approvals and clearances under the
Foreign Direct Investment Policy approved by Government of
India. Such companies/entities are permitted to raise fund
for meeting their equity and debt requirements from domestic
or offshore sources in accordance with the terms and
conditions stipulated by concerned authorities at the time
of their establishment in India. The decision regarding
financing of a particular economic activity or granting
loans to individual entities however, is taken by FIs
themselves based on their commercial judgement and the
lending policy laid down by their respective boards within
the framework of prudential regulations and exposure norms
prescribed by RBI from time to time. In accordance with the
practices and usages customary amongst the banks and
financial institution and in conformity with the provisions
of statues governing the financial institutions and the
provisions of the Public Financial Institutions (Obligation
as to fidelity and secrecy) Act, 1983, the information
relating to individual company/unit cannot be divulged.

records.title: ROHINI MIG SCHEME DELHI.
details:
(a) whether it is a fact that Rohini MIG Scheme for
 allotment of 90 square meters plots in Rohini, Delhi, was
 launched in 1981 but the scheme was not fully subscribed then;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the land earmarked
 for allotment of plots under the scheme has been diverted to
 other subsequent schemes, such as commercial complexes, flats,
 group housing etc; causing delay in allotment to original
 applicants;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) by when all original applicants are likely to get
 plots?

MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION
( SHRI JAGMOHAN )
(a): DDA in the year 1981 launched Rohini Residential Scheme
for allotment of MIG, LIG and Janta plots. As per the Scheme,
the registrants of MIG Category were to be allotted plots of the
size of 90 and 60 square metres. Under this scheme, 82,384
persons got themselves registered for allotment of plots
including 9,669 persons for allotment of plots of 90 square
metres under MIG category.
(b)&(c): No, Sir.
(d): No definite time-frame can be given for allotment of plots
to the remaining registrants at this stage. The process of
acquisition of land has since been initiated by the Govt. of
NCT of Delhi. As soon as the possession of the land so acquired
is handed over to the DDA, further action for allotment of plots
to the registrants will be taken after completing the process of
development.

records.title: ALLOTMENT OF PLOTS UNDER ROHINI MIG SCHEME .
details:
(a) the number of applicants registered for allotment of
 90 sq.mt. plot under Rohini MIG Scheme, 1981;
(b) the number of applicants who have been allotted 90
 sq.mt. plots;
(c) the reason for not alloting the plots to many
 applicants even after 19 years; and
(d) the steps being taken to liquidate the pending list?

MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION
( SHRI JAGMOHAN )
(a): DDA in the year 1981 launched Rohini Residential Scheme
for allotment of MIG, LIG and Janta plots. As per the Scheme,
the registrants of MIG category were to be allotted plots of the
size of 90 and 60 square metres. 9,669 applicants applied for
allotment of plots of 90 square metres under MIG category.
(b): 4,051 registrants have already been allotted plots of 90
square metres.
(c): Due to non-availability of land and lack of
infrastructural facilities to be provided by the Municipal
Corporation of Delhi, Delhi Jal Board, Delhi Vidyut Board, etc.
It has not been possible to allot plots to the remaining
registrants.
(d): It has been reported by the DDA that the process of
acquisition of land by the Land & Building Department of the
Government of NCT of Delhi has been initiated. As soon as the
possession of the land so acquired is handded over to the DDA,
further action for allotment of plots would be taken after
completing the process of development.
